a38.speaker: Environmental Justice Foundation (EJF) report
a38.speech: "North Koreans onboard were forced to work for as many as 10 years at sea — in some instances without ever stepping foot on land." ; "This would constitute forced labour of a magnitude that surpasses much of that witnessed in a global fishing industry already replete with abuse." ; Also said vessels carrying the North Koreans were involved in shark finning and capturing large marine animals such as dolphins, and potentially supplied markets in the EU, UK, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.

a38.speaker: Crew member (anonymous, quoted in EJF report)
a38.speech: "They never communicated with their wives or others while at sea, as they were not allowed to bring a mobile phone."

a38.speaker: Another crew member (anonymous, quoted in EJF report)
a38.speech: Said some North Koreans had worked on the vessel for "seven years, or eight years," adding: "They were not given permission to go home by their government."

a38.speaker: Steve Trent, CEO and founder of the Environmental Justice Foundation
a38.speech: "The impact of this situation is felt around the world: fish caught by this illegal labour force reaches seafood markets around the world." ; "China bears the brunt of the burden, but when products tainted by modern slavery end up on our plates, it is clear that flag states and regulators must also take full responsibility."

a38.speaker: Beijing (Chinese government)
a38.speech: Said it was "not aware" of the specific case.

a38.speaker: Lin Jian, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman
a38.speech: "China always requires its offshore fishing activities to abide by local laws and regulations and relevant provisions of international law." ; "Cooperation between China and North Korea is carried out in accordance with the framework of international law."

a38.speaker: US State Department
a38.speech: Said last year that an estimated 20,000 to 100,000 North Koreans work in China, primarily in restaurants and factories. ; According to a State Department report, North Korea withholds up to 90% of wages from its overseas workers, and imposes forced labour conditions on them.

a54.speaker: Ahmed Moalim Fiqi, Minister of Defence of the Federal Government of Somalia
a54.speech: Commended the Italian government's longstanding and vital support in strengthening Somalia's military capabilities, describing it as indispensable to the government's efforts to restore national security and stability. Expressed his deep appreciation for Italy's consistent support and reaffirmed Somalia's commitment to deepening this strategic relationship to help ensure lasting peace and security in the region.

a71.speaker: Save the Children (NGO)
a71.speech: Revealed the deaths of South Sudanese children last month, saying they were among the first directly linked to cuts ordered by US President Donald Trump, who slashed funding for global health programmes under his 'America First' policy. Had supported 27 health centres in Jonglei State until this year, when US cuts forced seven to close entirely and 20 to scale back operations, laying off about 200 of almost 600 staff nationwide; its budget for South Sudan is expected to drop to US$30m this year from US$50m last year.

a71.speaker: Christopher Nyamandi, Save the Children's country director in South Sudan
a71.speech: "There should be global moral outrage that the decisions made by powerful people in other countries have led to child deaths in just a matter of weeks."

a71.speaker: US State Department
a71.speech: Said it had no information about the reported deaths. A spokesperson insisted that many US-funded humanitarian projects in South Sudan remained operational but accused the country's leadership of misusing foreign aid: "While emergency lifesaving programmes continue, we will not, in good conscience, ask the American taxpayer to provide assistance that effectively subsidises the irresponsible and corrupt behaviour of South Sudan's political leaders."

a71.speaker: South Sudan's government
a71.speech: Has admitted to widespread corruption but denies specific allegations of graft, including against President Salva Kiir's family.

a71.speaker: UNICEF (UN Children's Fund)
a71.speech: Cited data showing a cholera outbreak was declared in South Sudan in October last year, with about 40,000 cases and 700 deaths recorded between September and March. About half of those stricken by the disease are children under 15.

a370.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a370.speech: Declared on Tuesday that his choice to build either multi-story buildings or huts is a personal affair: “Whether I build a hut, a tin-house, or a three- to four-story building, it is a personal matter; it has no bearing on the Somali mother who simply desires a free education for her child.”

a506.speaker: Government of Namibia
a506.speech: Namibia says it is able to continue its antiretroviral therapy (ART) programme despite the cut in USAID funds.

a506.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a506.speech: Experts fear negative effects on prevention measures and on care for vulnerable groups.

a506.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of Health (Namibia)
a506.speech: Stresses that Namibia had made provision with its own sustainability plan: "We recognised early on that donor funds would decline, and took measures to secure our progress" ; the Namibian government fully finances the procurement of antiretroviral medicines itself, while USAID funds had flowed above all into prevention programmes, community health workers and data collection.

a506.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of Health (Namibia)
a506.speech: "What will happen now is that people will have to wait longer for their medicines and counselling, because there is less support staff."

a506.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of Health (Namibia)
a506.speech: Assured that essential treatments such as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) will remain accessible to everyone: "In Namibia we provide health services without discrimination," he made clear, adding that this also applies to the LGBTQ community and other affected groups.

a506.speaker: Namibian Ministry of Health
a506.speech: With more than half a billion Namibian dollars from the state treasury, the Ministry of Health says it is convinced it can maintain ART provision, but that the challenges lie in financing the accompanying measures that are decisive for long-term control of the epidemic.

a548.speaker: Medical sources in Gaza
a548.speech: Reported on Wednesday that the death toll from the Israeli aggression on the Gaza Strip has risen to 50,183 Palestinians, while the number of wounded has reached 113,828 since October 2023 ; indicated that since 18 March, 830 people have been killed and 1,787 others wounded ; added that 39 martyrs, including one recovered body, and 124 wounded people arrived at hospitals in the Gaza Strip in the last hours ; explained that a number of martyrs remain under the rubble of destroyed homes and facilities and on the roads, and that ambulance crews are unable to reach them because of a lack of resources.

a704.speaker: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (official commitment statement)
a704.speech: Has committed for decades "to promoting sustainable development in middle- and low-income countries and to reducing the economic gap that keeps countries under the yoke of poverty, undermines their capacity to meet the needs of vulnerable groups, and prevents their equal access to resources." ; "Acting on behalf of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Centre has helped relieve the suffering of millions of people in need around the world."

a704.speaker: A. Check Ibrahim Kontao, Director of the NGO Al-Farouk
a704.speech: At the launch of the distribution of food kits to 43,400 beneficiaries, said the King Salman Centre is a leading organisation in the field of humanitarian aid worldwide: "It strives to provide high-quality support to the most vulnerable categories in more than 100 countries around the world. The Centre has already implemented humanitarian projects in Mali in the areas of water and sanitation, food security, health and education. This support reinforces the values of generosity and benevolence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, both at the level of its leadership and of its people, values passed down from generation to generation. It is an illustration of the Islamic fraternity invoked." ; Pledged to carry out the projects financed by the King Salman Centre for Relief and Humanitarian Aid with the required quality, honouring the Centre's reputation and international standing: "That is, while scrupulously respecting the values and principles governing humanitarian work. This mission will be accomplished with professionalism and integrity, God willing."

a704.speaker: A beneficiary of the Saudi meat donation (anonymous)
a704.speech: "Truly, it is a great joy for us. Thanks to this donation, many families will be able to eat meat with dignity, especially at this end-of-year period. This gift from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Mali is not surprising to us since these are two brotherly and friendly countries. And Saudi Arabia has always respected this tradition. We take this opportunity to salute and thank the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman, and the Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for this humanitarian gesture towards the Malian people."

a704.speaker: An official of the National Directorate of Social Development (unnamed)
a704.speech: "We are here today for the distribution of the donation offered by our Saudi friends and brothers. On behalf of the President of the Transition, the Prime Minister and the Minister of Health and Social Development, this donation of mutton carcasses from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to the State of Mali falls within the framework of traditions going back several years. Saudi Arabia makes this donation to Mali after the Hajj that preceded it." ; "This donation is an important support in the current context. We believe it will serve the populations who really need it. So it is for needy populations and only for needy populations, it is important to recall that."

a921.speaker: Edwin Makwati, University of Botswana law lecturer (court papers)
a921.speech: Accuses Norris of varying the decision of the Academic Disciplinary Committee (ADC) to expel one Tshepang Mabaila, a student reading for a Bachelor of Laws Degree at the University of Botswana ; has approached court seeking it to review and set aside the VC’s decision to register Mabaila as a student for the Bachelor of Laws for the second semester of the 2023/2024 academic year, and to review and set aside the decision by the VC to vary the sanction of expulsion recommended by the ADC to a suspension of four semesters ; also seeks an Order to have the Vice Chancellor render a written guarantee of non-repetition and an apology to the University of Botswana student community and citizens of Botswana for favouritism, maladministration and disregard for orderliness.

a921.speaker: Prof David Norris, University of Botswana Vice Chancellor (answering affidavit)
a921.speech: Says Edwin Makwati acted prematurely ; contends that in terms of the UB’s Academic Policy, the DADC has no authority at all to impose a sanction of a written reprimand, and that a written reprimand shall normally be imposed only for misconduct that has no bearing on the performance in the examinations ; avers that the ADC has no authority to make a recommendation of an additional penalty of expulsion in terms of paragraph 3.1.6 of the Academic Policy.

a921.speaker: Prof David Norris, University of Botswana Vice Chancellor (answering affidavit)
a921.speech: Contends that Makwati has no legal standing to institute these proceedings and seek the relief he does, because he does not have a direct and substantial interest in the VC’s impugned decision; that the only person with a direct and substantial interest is Mabaila, whom the applicant has not joined as a party to the proceedings; and that Makwati was not a member of the ADC whose recommendation for Mabaila’s expulsion he has varied, and therefore has no legal standing to bring the proceedings to court.

a921.speaker: Prof David Norris, University of Botswana Vice Chancellor (answering affidavit)
a921.speech: Avers that the decision to allow Mabaila to register for the second semester of the 2023/2024 academic period was not made by him as the university’s chief executive officer, but by the Department of Academic Services, and that if Makwati contends that the DAS decision to re-admit Mabaila was unfair, unlawful and unreasonable and stands to be reviewed and set aside, then he is under obligation to join the Director of DAS, who is the “decision-maker” in respect of such decision, in the proceedings.

a921.speaker: Prof David Norris, University of Botswana Vice Chancellor (answering affidavit)
a921.speech: Contends that a significant portion of the relief sought by Makwati has been overtaken by events and therefore rendered moot, purely academic and unenforceable — for example the relief to review and set aside the decision to allow Mabaila to register for the second semester of 2023/2024, since that semester came to an end on 26 July 2024 ; contends that the relief seeking a written guarantee of non-repetition and an apology falls far outside the purview of the court in determining the relevant issues in respect of review proceedings.

a921.speaker: Departmental Academic Disciplinary Committee (DADC) (record of proceedings filed in court)
a921.speech: Found Mabaila guilty of academic misconduct after determining that he had paid another student, Laone Campbell Lekganyane, the sum of P1,000 to impersonate him for the purposes of writing examination papers for LLB courses LAW 201, LAW 235, LAW 236 and LAW 237 during the second semester of the 2022/2023 Academic period — a crime Mabaila owned up to — and imposed a sanction of a written reprimand and the loss of credits of the courses that had been the subject of the examinations.

a921.speaker: Academic Disciplinary Committee (ADC) (recommendation to the Vice Chancellor)
a921.speech: Dealt with Mabaila’s matter and made a recommendation that an additional penalty of expulsion from UB be imposed.

a930.speaker: Shatiso Nlebgwa, attorney for Nnewe (statutory notice to sue dated November 25, 2014)
a930.speech: Stated that his client was arrested by Kutlwano police officers on February 5 in 2014.

a961.speaker: Peter Magosi, Director-General of the Directorate of Intelligence and Security (DIS), and Solomon Mantswe, Deputy Police Commissioner Operations
a961.speech: held a meeting at Peleng kgotla to update residents on the ongoing investigation of the Karema boy’s murder.

a961.speaker: Residents of Lobatse
a961.speech: could not contain their anger when being updated on the latest developments of the case by Mantswe, shouting in protest and demanding answers.

a988.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (Monthly Economic Review for June 2025)
a988.speech: Data show that total revenues for the quarter from April 1 to June 30 stood at K1.17 trillion while expenditures were recorded at K1.84 trillion, creating a K669 billion deficit; the report indicates the budget deficit stood at K130.4 billion in April, rose to K300 billion in May and dropped to K238.9 billion in June. RBM attributed the rise in the budget deficit to the decline in both tax and non-tax revenues and some expenditure pressure which intensified in May: “Revenues decreased by K86.7 billion to K348.4 billion in May 2025 from K435.1 billion in the preceding month. The outturn was driven by decreases in tax revenues, non-tax revenues and grant collections by K54.8 billion, K23.6 billion and K8.3 billion to K260.7 billion, K29.5 billion and K58.2 billion, respectively.” The report further said government expenditures increased by K82.8 billion to K648.4 billion in May 2025 on account of increases in recurrent and other expenditures while development expenditure decreased by K11.2 billion to K112.1 billion.

a988.speaker: Bertha Bangara-Chikadza, Economics Association of Malawi acting president
a988.speech: Described the quarterly deficit as a concern, saying government’s fiscal pressure mainly heightens in the coming quarters of the economic lean period: “It would be reasonable to expect that the quarterly deficit should have been lower if the government was to achieve the planned deficit for the year.” Said the current situation underscores the challenges government is facing to fulfil its mandate effectively.

a988.speaker: Agnes Nyirongo, Centre for Social Concern economic governance officer
a988.speech: Said the reduction in development expenditure threatens to derail long-term poverty reduction efforts: “If we continue increasing recurrent costs, largely salaries and administrative overheads while cutting investments in health, education and infrastructure, we are simply locking ourselves into a low-growth, high-inequality future.”

a988.speaker: Alick Nyasulu, economic statistician
a988.speech: Cautioned that rising government deficits coupled with the foreign aid and debt squeeze will force the government to borrow more from the domestic market, and warned that this would worsen the crowding out effect, a situation where the private sector cannot access loans from commercial banks.

a988.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a988.speech: Projected that the government will close the 2025/26 financial year with a fiscal deficit of K2.47 trillion or 9.5 percent of GDP, which will be primarily financed through domestic borrowing amounting to K2.33 trillion and foreign borrowing of K145.78 billion.

a1163.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a1163.speech: Warned on Wednesday that nearly 300,000 civilians are now trapped in El Fasher, the besieged capital of North Darfur, where hunger and violence are reaching a critical level; the UN agency says it is still waiting for security guarantees in order to deliver its humanitarian aid to El Fasher, a city now on the brink of famine; according to WFP the population of El Fasher – still under the control of the Sudanese army – is suffering an extreme food shortage ; "Families are running out of options and time," the agency warned on the social network X, specifying that its aid convoys remain blocked for lack of authorisation ; WFP estimates that it needs 645 million dollars to maintain its assistance in Sudan over the next six months and calls on all parties to the conflict to guarantee safe and unhindered access to the populations trapped by war and hunger.

a1163.speaker: United Nations Security Council
a1163.speech: Said it was "gravely concerned" by the siege imposed by the RSF on El Fasher, also denouncing the establishment of a parallel authority by the paramilitaries, seen as a threat to the country's unity.

a1163.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (office)
a1163.speech: Reports massacres in several displacement camps, notably at Abu Shouk, where 57 civilians were killed on 11 August, including 40 inside the camp itself.

a1163.speaker: Volker Türk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1163.speech: Condemned "repeated and unacceptable attacks" targeting civilians and spoke of grave violations of international humanitarian law.

a1163.speaker: Refugees in Chad (testimonies)
a1163.speech: Testimonies gathered in Chad from refugees describe murders, gang rapes and enforced disappearances during the attacks carried out by the RSF.

a1430.speaker: Billboard
a1430.speech: As reported by Billboard, two contributors to 'Water' have filed a lawsuit alleging they were unfairly excluded from proper royalty payments due to what they describe as a "nefarious" plan orchestrated by one of the track's main producers.

a1430.speaker: Olmo Zucca and Jackson LoMastro, California-based songwriters (lawsuit/court filing)
a1430.speech: The lawsuit claims that Awuku intentionally sidelined them by signing an exclusive deal with Tyla to take sole credit for the song's production, offering the pair only 10% each in publishing royalties while keeping 15% for himself; the court filing further cites that the plaintiffs tried for months to resolve the matter with Awuku, but he refused to cooperate; according to the complaint, Awuku allegedly hid his involvement in the song's creation and duped them into agreeing to a lower royalty rate; the plaintiffs claim they only discovered the truth in a May 2024 meeting with Epic Records President Ezekiel Lewis, where they learned Awuku had never told the label about any co-producers.

a1430.speaker: Olmo Zucca and Jackson LoMastro, plaintiffs (complaint)
a1430.speech: Are seeking official producer credits on the track and want their royalty rate adjusted to 12.5%, both retroactively and moving forward, and are also requesting a producer fee. "Because the defendants have refused to recognise the plaintiffs' status as top-line producers of the song and have failed to pay the plaintiffs all the royalties owed to them, the plaintiffs have each suffered injury in fact," the complaint reads; Zucca and LoMastro claim that being left out of the credits has cost them more than just money, and that it has also harmed their reputations and closed doors to new opportunities in the industry; additionally, the suit states that 'Water' has generated over US$10 million in revenue since its release, with estimated earnings potentially exceeding US$50 million.

a1430.speaker: Tyla, singer (non-response)
a1430.speech: The lawsuit names Tyla as a defendant; however, it does not allege any misconduct on her part. She also has not made any public comments on the matter.

a1515.speaker: Upper Nile authorities (statement)
a1515.speech: Said the delegation, which included German Ambassador Christian Sedat and representatives from various UN and international organizations, met with Governor James Odhok in Malakal, and that they discussed gaps and challenges resulting from the pause in humanitarian aid.

a1515.speaker: Germany
a1515.speech: Reiterated its commitment to collaborate with the government in supporting relief initiatives, being the second-largest donor of humanitarian assistance to South Sudan.

a1515.speaker: Government sources in Upper Nile State
a1515.speech: Said the situation has already affected normal operations of some UN agencies facilitating transportation of South Sudanese returnees from Upper Nile to different parts of the country.

a1515.speaker: IOM representative among the delegation (unnamed)
a1515.speech: Said the agency has temporarily halted some of its activities in the State awaiting further directives.

a1515.speaker: Anita Kiki Gbeho, Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary General in South Sudan
a1515.speech: Acknowledged the worsening humanitarian situation caused by flooding, conflict and the influx of refugees ; "We know this state has also received people who have crossed from Sudan, but more importantly, it was to hear from him and to brief the delegation so that they can be a mouthpiece for South Sudan when they go back to their countries" ; "We know that the situation is difficult. Unity State is plagued by flooding, they have to deal with displacement, they have an IDPs camp with hundreds of thousands of individuals who need support on daily basis."

a1515.speaker: Amb. Deike Potzel, Director for Crisis Prevention at the German Embassy
a1515.speech: Pledged her country's enduring support to alleviate the humanitarian crisis in the country and underscored that last year alone Germany provided 60 million U.S. dollars for humanitarian response in South Sudan ; "It is also a great opportunity to underline our support for South Sudanese people. We have been very steadfast in our support." ; "I want to assure you that we will continue to support the humanitarian response here. But this visit is also an opportunity to thank the governor and the people of the state for welcoming refugees coming in from Sudan."

a1619.speaker: United Nations
a1619.speech: Expressed its gratitude to Morocco following King Mohammed VI's decision to send a new shipment of humanitarian aid to the population of Gaza, which has been struck by famine and the Israeli blockade.

a1619.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco
a1619.speech: Ordered the dispatch of 100 tonnes of food and medicine, to be delivered by air "directly and urgently" to the Palestinians, in continuity with previous convoys already sent by Rabat since the beginning of the conflict.

a1619.speaker: Stéphane Dujarric, spokesman for the UN Secretary-General
a1619.speech: Described the Moroccan decision as "generous": "We welcome the generosity and the decision of His Majesty King Mohammed VI to send significant humanitarian aid to the population of Gaza," he said, stressing that the residents of the enclave "lack everything: food, medicine, shelter" ; calling on the international community to "do as much as possible" to facilitate the delivery of relief, he insisted on the need to press for an immediate ceasefire.

a1619.speaker: United Nations
a1619.speech: Also deplores the blockade imposed since 18 March by Israeli forces, which prevents the regular entry of aid.

a1619.speaker: Humanitarian organisations
a1619.speech: According to them, the blockade has already caused the deaths of more than 269 people, including 112 children, from hunger and the absence of care.

a1619.speaker: Morocco (Rabat)
a1619.speech: Intends to maintain its commitment in the face of what Rabat describes as a "serious and catastrophic" humanitarian crisis.

a1640.speaker: Democratic Movement of Mozambique (MDM), political party
a1640.speech: Promises to build houses for young people, jobs and an increase in the subsidy for the elderly ; In the City of Maputo, in its interaction with potential voters in the Laulane neighbourhood, Kamavota Municipal District, the MDM promised jobs for young people and an improvement in the quality of education in the country, should it win the elections of 9 October.

a1640.speaker: Lutero Simango, MDM presidential candidate
a1640.speech: Promises to raise the elderly subsidy from the current 600 to 1,200 meticais and to mobilise investors for the construction of small units for processing and preserving fresh produce. These promises were made this Monday to the population of Nhamatanda district, Sofala province.

a1640.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Frelimo presidential candidate
a1640.speech: Promises the establishment of farms in Maringue to capitalise on the district's agricultural potential and generate employment. Also this Monday, Chapo was in Gorongosa, Sofala, where he promised to erect a peace monument, an operating theatre at the local hospital, and secondary schools for young people.

a1640.speaker: Renamo, political party (City of Maputo)
a1640.speech: Promises to build decent schools and to pay a maintenance allowance for the elderly, should Issufo Momade win the elections.

a1640.speaker: Joaquim Chissano, former President of the Republic of Mozambique
a1640.speech: Says that all vital forces must be guided by tolerance and serenity in the ongoing electoral process. Chissano likewise welcomed the order and calm that have characterised the election campaign so far.

a1640.speaker: Municipal Council of Maputo (Edilidade)
a1640.speech: Promises to change the scenario in which around five thousand stalls stand empty in the municipal markets of the city of Maputo while hundreds of people trade on the pavements around those same markets, even competing for the streets with vehicles.

a1830.speaker: Donald Trump, Republican presidential candidate and former US president
a1830.speech: Claimed in a wide-ranging interview with the Wall Street Journal that he threatened to strike Moscow if Russian President Vladimir Putin launched an attack on Ukraine; asked whether he would use military force to respond to a potential blockade of Taiwan by Beijing, said he would not have to, as his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, "respects me and he knows I'm … crazy"; said the same is true of Putin, who he claimed to have an excellent relationship with, and that at one point he told him: "Vladimir, if you go after Ukraine, I am going to hit you so hard, you're not even going to believe it. I'm going to hit you right in the middle of fricking Moscow… We're friends. I don't want to do it, but I have no choice." ; said that when Putin reacted with disbelief, he responded "Way... You're going to be hit so hard, and I'm going to take those … domes right off your head."

a1830.speaker: Donald Trump, Republican presidential candidate and former US president
a1830.speech: Has repeatedly said that the Russia-Ukraine conflict would not have happened had he been in office, and has vowed to end it within 24 hours if elected.

a1830.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President (as reported by Trump)
Public records
a1830.speech: According to public records, Putin last spoke with Trump in 2020.

a1830.speaker: Bob Woodward, American journalist
a1830.speech: Claimed that the two have had "maybe as many as seven" conversations since Trump left the White House.

a1830.speaker: The Kremlin and the Trump campaign
a1830.speech: Have both denied the claim that Trump and Putin have spoken since Trump left the White House.

a1830.speaker: J.D. Vance, Trump's running mate
a1830.speech: Said Trump could start talks with Russia, Ukraine, and European stakeholders to establish a demilitarised zone along the current front line, with Kiev agreeing to stay out of Nato.

a1845.speaker: United States Embassy in South Sudan (statement)
a1845.speech: Condemned an alleged attack on a World Food Programme boat in New Fangak, Jonglei State, reportedly carried out by personnel of the South Sudan People's Defence Forces; said SSPDF personnel raided the boat on September 7 and stole food and other supplies intended for civilians facing hunger; noted the stolen goods were replaced on September 20 but described the attack as part of a worsening pattern of looting and extortion targeting humanitarian aid by armed groups. It called on the transitional government to prevent attacks on aid operations and to ensure access to populations at risk of famine, including in Upper Nile State: "We call upon South Sudan's leaders, at all levels, to prevent such actions and to be a partner to those - including international donors - seeking to help the South Sudanese people. We urge the transitional government to create conditions that will end the country's humanitarian crisis."

a1845.speaker: United States Embassy in South Sudan (statement)
a1845.speech: "We are increasingly concerned about the inability of implementing partners delivering humanitarian assistance to reach conflict-affected populations in Upper Nile State, due to humanitarian access denials by transitional government officials in areas which face a possible risk of famine. Urgent humanitarian intervention is required in these areas, and government authorities must facilitate access." The US mission also urged leaders to address the high costs and risks that hinder aid delivery and to guarantee unhindered access for humanitarian organizations.

a1845.speaker: Major General Lul Ruai Koang, SSPDF Spokesperson
a1845.speech: Said the army is yet to receive an official complaint from the US Embassy.

a2091.speaker: Jutta Urpilainen, EU Commissioner for International Partnerships
a2091.speech: Was on record last week urging a shared position between member states to effect "any real influence" on the Ethiopian government.

a2091.speaker: European Union
a2091.speech: Europe says it wants to give the five support items lined up for disbursement some thought before releasing them; the EU, in particular, calls for full humanitarian access for relief actors "to reach people in need in all affected areas".

a2091.speaker: EU spokesperson (anonymous, speaking to devex.com)
a2091.speech: Payments to the government will only be unblocked once certain conditions are met, according to an EU spokesperson who talked to www.devex.com.

a2091.speaker: Diplomatic sources (anonymous, spoke to Fortune)
a2091.speech: All 27 member states are on the same page about the problems in Tigray and the difficult conditions there; the nature of the responses advocated by Brussels, nonetheless, face strong resistance from Italy and France.

a2091.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia (Twitter post)
a2091.speech: Had uplifting words to say on Twitter two weeks ago after speaking with German Chancellor Angela Merkel; describing his conversation as a "good phone call," the Prime Minister said the two leaders spoke on "national and regional issue[s]" and "strengthening development and economic cooperation between #Ethiopia and Germany."

a2091.speaker: Official from the German Ministry of Foreign Affairs (tweet)
a2091.speech: "The Chancellor emphasised the importance of a peaceful solution to the conflict in the Tigray region and the humanitarian care of the people affected in the conflict area. Humanitarian aid organisations and the media must be given free access to the Tigray region."

a2091.speaker: Spokesperson, Germany's Ministry of Economic Cooperation & Development (responding to devex.com)
a2091.speech: "Germany is willing to continue supporting Ethiopia. The Ethiopian government remains committed to its reform process, even since the start of the conflict in Tigray." ; disclosed Berlin's own conditions to be met before further funds are disbursed, pointing out that his government wants to take a long-term view of development in Ethiopia, wants to encourage the start of a "credible political process aimed at resolving the conflict in Tigray," and wants to see as a final condition "the conclusion of debt rescheduling negotiations between Ethiopia and China."

a2091.speaker: European Commission / Brussels
a2091.speech: Believes appeals for debt relief, submitted by Ethiopia, Chad and Zambia, should have a decision based on "technical analysis rather than politics".

a2146.speaker: Geir Pedersen, Special Envoy of the United Nations Secretary-General for Syria
a2146.speech: Announced, at a press conference held on Sunday, that the work of the fourth session of the small body of the Constitutional Committee on Syria would focus on national foundations and principles.

a2146.speaker: United Nations Security Council Resolution 2254 (document)
a2146.speech: Called for a ceasefire and a political settlement in Syria; demanded that all parties immediately cease any attacks against civilian targets, urged all member states to support efforts to achieve a ceasefire, and asked the UN to convene the parties to engage in formal negotiations in early January 2016; it also stressed that free and fair elections would be held under United Nations supervision and that the political transition would be Syrian-led.

a2146.speaker: Joint declaration on the sidelines of the third round of the Syrian Constitutional Committee (August)
a2146.speech: Underlined attachment to Syria's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.

a2146.speaker: Participants in the Geneva talks
a2146.speech: All participants agreed to support efforts to find a solution in Syria on the basis of United Nations Security Council resolution 2254 ; the co-chairs agreed to hold the fifth round on 5 January 2021, if the health situation permits.

a2231.speaker: Indonesian authorities
a2231.speech: In a last-minute reversal late Wednesday, they clarified the embargo would include all exports of the oilseed and not only products intended for edible oils, as indicated a day earlier.

a2231.speaker: Airlangga Hartarto, Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs
a2231.speech: "All products," including crude palm oil, "are covered by the Ministry of Trade regulation and will be enforced."

a2231.speaker: Joko Widodo, President of Indonesia
a2231.speech: Said supplying the country's 270 million residents was the "highest priority" of his government ; "As the world's largest palm oil producer, it is ironic that we are having difficulties getting cooking oil."

a2231.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation
a2231.speech: According to it, vegetable oils are among a number of staple food items that have seen prices hit record highs in recent weeks, following Russia's invasion of agricultural powerhouse Ukraine.

a2370.speaker: Israel Defense Forces and Palestinian authorities
a2370.speech: Said that the Rafah crossing, located south of Gaza City, had been taken by Israeli tanks belonging to an armoured brigade.

a2370.speaker: Israeli army
a2370.speech: Said it had decided to take control of the crossing after receiving information that it was "being used for terrorist purposes" by the Palestinian Islamist movement Hamas, though without providing any evidence.

a2370.speaker: Israeli forces
a2370.speech: Had previously alleged that Hamas had used the area around the border to launch dozens of missiles that killed four Israeli soldiers near Kerem Shalom, which links south-eastern Gaza to Israeli territory.

a2370.speaker: Wael Abu Omar, spokesman for the border authority in the Gaza Strip government controlled by Hamas since 2007
a2370.speech: Said that the Rafah crossing, the main entry point for humanitarian aid, was closed. "The entire western area [of Rafah] has become a theatre of operations since yesterday [Monday]. The bombardment has not stopped," said Abu Omar, adding that border personnel had fled because of the Israeli offensive.

a2370.speaker: Israeli army
a2370.speech: On Monday night, said it had killed 20 Hamas militants in "targeted strikes" in the eastern area of Rafah, where three tunnel networks belonging to the Islamist group were discovered.

a2370.speaker: Israeli War Cabinet, headed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
a2370.speech: Announced on Monday that it had decided to press ahead with the offensive in Rafah, while at the same time agreeing to continue negotiations for a truce with Hamas.

a2500.speaker: To Lam, General Secretary of the Vietnam Communist Party
a2500.speech: "All the Vietnamese are the descendants of Vietnam. They have the rights to live and work, to have freedom to pursue happiness and love in this country." ; "In a spirit of closing the past, respecting differences, aiming for the future, the whole party, the people and the army vow to make Vietnam become a country of peace, unity, prosperity and development."

a2500.speaker: To Lam, General Secretary of the Vietnam Communist Party
a2500.speech: Said that beyond a victory over the U.S. and South Vietnam, the fall of Saigon was a "glorious landmark" that ended a 30-year fight for independence that began with the fight to oust French colonial troops; he said Vietnam owes its position in the world today to support from the Soviet Union, China and solidarity from Laos and Cambodia, as well as "progressive" people all over the world including the U.S.

a2500.speaker: Nguyen Thi Hue, spectator and Ho Chi Minh City resident
a2500.speech: "Now it's time for peace. Peace is the dream that everyone in the world wants."

a2500.speaker: Nguyen Khac Giang, analyst at Singapore's ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute
a2500.speech: Said the emphasis on reconciliation and not, like previous years, on military victory reflected how Vietnam was approaching the changing tides of the global economy and geopolitics today; added that the Vietnam War remains central to how the Communist Party framed its legitimacy, not just as a military triumph but also as a symbol of national unity ; "The war still defines Vietnam's unity, and its unresolved divides."

a2500.speaker: Pham Ngoc Son, 69-year-old veteran who fought for the communists
a2500.speech: Said that today there is "only space for peace and friendship" between the U.S. and Vietnam ; "The war is over a long time ago."

a2500.speaker: Huong Le-Thu, International Crisis Group think tank
a2500.speech: Said Vietnam being slammed with reciprocal tariffs of 46%, one of the highest, puts a "big question mark" on what the U.S. wants to achieve in Asia; said that previously, close ties with Washington have helped Vietnam balance its relations with its much larger and more powerful neighbour China ; "It really will be shaping up (on) how the new administration sees the strategic picture in the Indo-Pacific and where countries like Vietnam would fit in."

a2500.speaker: Tammy Bruce, U.S. State Department spokeswoman
a2500.speech: Refused to comment on reports that the Trump administration had discouraged diplomats from attending anniversary events: "I'm not going to discuss what has been suggested or not suggested."

a2500.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Hanoi
a2500.speech: Said U.S. consul general in Ho Chi Minh City Susan Burns had attended the event.

a2500.speaker: Vietnamese officials
a2500.speech: Say the relationship with the U.S. is anchored in American efforts to address war legacies such as Agent Orange contamination and unexploded ordnance in the countryside that still threaten lives.

a2521.speaker: Debt Management Office (DMO) of Nigeria
a2521.speech: has reported that the nation's total public debt reached approximately N144.67 trillion (equivalent to $94.2 billion USD) by the end of December 2024, a substantial increase from the N121.67 trillion ($91.46 billion USD) recorded in the first quarter of the same year.

a2521.speaker: Nigerian government
a2521.speech: has formally requested approval for an additional $24.14 billion in foreign loans, which if approved would further escalate the nation's total public debt to over N182.91 trillion.

a2521.speaker: The World Bank and the IMF
a2521.speech: have assessed Nigeria's debt stock as manageable, but they are not comfortable with the acknowledgement that debt servicing presents a substantial challenge due to the country's low tax revenue generation.

a2569.speaker: Cyriaque Edouard Dossa, magistrate, doctor of law (presentation at the FONAC/USAID international seminar on transnational crime and gender)
a2569.speech: Presented a paper on the theme “Transnational organised crime: what implications for human rights and the development of a nation?” and set the scene with tangible realities: “In those places [the Zongo and Sekandji neighbourhoods in Cotonou and Seme-Podji] you will find vehicles and above all vehicle parts that in principle can only be obtained on order from the parent company. But, given that these accessories are often the fruit of theft in this country, as is also often the case abroad — take the cases of Nigeria and even of the European states of origin. These parts are often the product of armed robbery, of loss of human life, of loss of the right to property, of the right to free movement, which are nothing other than human rights.”

a2569.speaker: Cyriaque Edouard Dossa, magistrate
a2569.speech: Observed of legislative and presidential elections in Africa that “candidates spend billions of our francs without seeking to know the origin of the said funds, most of which is laundered capital. Once in power, experience seems to show that their first reflexes are not along the lines of development but of satisfying their benefactors, an attitude that dangerously compromises the future of nations”; and questioned the proliferation of deposit banks in Benin, wondering with what purse the depositors go there.

a2569.speaker: Cyriaque Edouard Dossa, magistrate
a2569.speech: Observed that the opening of borders, the free movement of capital and goods and the development of telecommunications also reveal the use of the various channels of globalisation for criminal ends; noted that the lack of regulation of economic and financial activities on an international scale gives criminal phenomena, once confined within a territory, immeasurable possibilities of expansion, so that criminality has become more systematically collective and makes light of borders — this is transnational organised crime.

a2569.speaker: Cyriaque Edouard Dossa, magistrate
a2569.speech: Said the term “Organised Cross-border Crime” is not an offence but should be understood as “a lodge, a consortium, a federation of offences whose list is not exhaustive”; explained that “the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime retains a few of them, including money laundering and corruption, supported by many mechanisms for successful repression such as international cooperation for the purposes of confiscation, extradition, transfer of sentenced persons and mutual legal assistance; all of these are assets for achieving an effective fight against this college of deviances that falls within the net of transnational organised crime” ; noted that “the expression ‘organised crime’ was born in the United States in the 1920s… in a police report during the Prohibition period… the most famous figure being that of Al Capone”, and that since then many authors have prematurely announced that the notion cannot be grasped.

a2569.speaker: Maurice Cusson (cited definition)
a2569.speech: Considers that “by organised crime is generally meant a structured and hierarchical association of professional criminals obeying binding rules and methodically planning the illicit enterprises that they monopolise through the systematic use of violence.”

a2569.speaker: Raymond Gassin (cited definition)
a2569.speech: Considers that “organised crime means crime whose preparation and execution are characterised by methodical organisation and which, most often, provides its perpetrators with their means of subsistence.”

a2569.speaker: Michel Quille (cited definition, aligned with the US 1967 preparatory work for the Crime Control Act of 1970)
a2569.speech: “Organised crime is a society that seeks to carry out its activities outside the control of citizens and their government. Its action is not improvised but results from very complex conspiracies hatched over many years and intended to secure control of a complete field of activity with a view to accumulating the greatest possible profits.”

a2569.speaker: Raphaël Parizot (cited analysis)
a2569.speech: Analyses that “organised crime is a modern form of delinquency that is difficult to pin down.”

a2569.speaker: Gilles Favarel-Garrigues, researcher (cited)
a2569.speech: Wonders whether transnational organised crime is not a concept to be buried, on account of the difficulty of defining its contours.

a2569.speaker: United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime of December 2000 (Palermo Convention)
a2569.speech: States that “organised criminal group means a structured group of three or more persons, existing for a period of time and acting in concert with the aim of committing one or more serious crimes or offences established in accordance with this Convention, in order to obtain, directly or indirectly, a financial or other material benefit”, and that “serious crime means conduct constituting an offence punishable by a maximum deprivation of liberty of at least four years or a more serious penalty.”

a2569.speaker: Cyriaque Edouard Dossa, magistrate
a2569.speech: Stated that transnational organised crime encompasses practically all serious profit-motivated criminal activities of an international character, listing drug, arms and human trafficking, clandestine migration, financial and economic crime, cybercrime, corruption, tax fraud and evasion, money laundering, hostage-taking, maritime piracy and terrorism as the most frequent in West Africa; noted that cybercrime’s most profitable area for criminals is identity theft, generating about 1 billion dollars each year, and that criminals increasingly exploit the Internet to steal private data, access bank accounts and fraudulently obtain payment card details.

a2569.speaker: Experts in the field (cited by the magistrate)
a2569.speech: Estimate that between 30 and 40 tonnes of cocaine from South America transit through West Africa each year.

a2569.speaker: UNODC
a2569.speech: Discovered between 2009 and 2012 drug factories, notably of methamphetamine, in Guinea-Bissau, Guinea-Conakry and Nigeria.

a2569.speaker: United Nations mission (report cited by the magistrate)
a2569.speech: “Already in the mid-1990s, a United Nations mission estimated that eight million small arms and light weapons must have been in free circulation in West Africa, outside state control. This situation was aggravated in the 2000s by the Ivorian crisis of 2002 and above all by the Libyan crisis of 2011.”

a2569.speaker: NATO (cited)
a2569.speech: Reported the disappearance of at least 10,000 missiles that could constitute a mortal danger both for Libya’s neighbouring countries and for the regions frequented by terrorists, notably the Sahel-Sahara and the Horn of Africa.

a2569.speaker: International Labour Organization (ILO)
a2569.speech: Estimated, in the recent past, that the number of trafficking victims was, at any given moment, about 2.4 million, with profits of about 32 billion dollars.

a2569.speaker: Cyriaque Edouard Dossa, magistrate
a2569.speech: Said the international community has always made the fight against transnational organised crime a major challenge, adopting several instruments including the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime of December 2000, the United Nations Convention against Corruption, the UN Convention of 15 December 1997 for the Suppression of Terrorist Bombings and Security Council resolutions on terrorism, supported at African level by African Union, ECOWAS and UEMOA texts and by the African Centre for the Study and Research on Terrorism (CAERT) in Algiers; stressed that several West African states have over the past dozen years adopted domestic laws on drug and precursor control under the 1988 Vienna Convention, uniform anti-money-laundering laws, and laws suppressing terrorism and its financing, corruption and related offences.

a2673.speaker: Rin Tueny Mabor, Lakes State Governor
a2673.speech: Has encouraged the state residents to prioritize agricultural production and promised to help provide security for them to freely go about their businesses ; encouraged citizens including those in the urban areas to find land and prepare for farming ahead of the rainy season in order to tackle hunger, which he sees as a key factor driving conflicts in the state ; in his new year message, promised security for farmers while calling on all communities to engage in extensive agricultural production for both business and subsistence: "There is nothing that will sustain us except agriculture. Go out to the villages and start clearances farms this time to establish farms." ; "The people tried it in 2024, but it is not enough. The production of 2024 should be the seeds of 2025 farming. I want you people to farm for what you will eat and sell the surplus." ; "Do it yourself and your government will provide security for you. I want you to eradicate hunger because hunger makes people hate each other. Its promotes reckless talk and violence."

a2673.speaker: President Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a2673.speech: Said the government would embark on agriculture to enhance food security, while assuring the country of his commitment to address hunger ; directed the Ministry of Agriculture to redouble its efforts and support the farmers across the country to boost and improve productivity.

a2673.speaker: Rin Tueny Mabor, Lakes State Governor
a2673.speech: Further pointed out that peace dialogues have been initiated between neighboring Tonj East, and Tonj North counties of Warrap State, and Pakam in Rumbek North and Cueibet in Lakes State.

a2673.speaker: UN agencies
a2673.speech: Have warned of an alarming humanitarian crisis in South Sudan where more than half the country's population will go hungry in 2025.

a3462.speaker: Government of India (statement)
a3462.speech: “As part of India's humanitarian outreach, ICGS Sachet is carrying 20 metric tonnes of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) material, including medical stores and medicines, to be handed over to Mozambican authorities,” read a statement issued by the Indian government.

a3462.speaker: India in Mozambique (@IndiainMoz), Indian High Commission social media post
a3462.speech: “Gifting of medicines and equipment to Mozambique (11 Oct 2025) ... gifted medicines and equipment to [Mozambique], which will augment healthcare capabilities. The first tranche of medicines and equipment, brought by ICGS Sachet, was handed over to the Hon'ble Health Minister in Maputo.”

a3672.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a3672.speech: Called for urgent diplomatic intervention to reopen Goma International Airport and Kavumu Airport in Bukavu, DRC, during the opening of the virtual extraordinary summit of SADC Heads of State and Government; stated that reopening the airports is essential to facilitate humanitarian assistance and enable SADC and its structures to find an immediate and effective solution for its mission.

a3672.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a3672.speech: Described the invasion of DRC territory by M23 and their external supporters, as well as the establishment of de facto authorities and illegitimate parallel administrations in some areas, as serious violations of international law; noted that these acts demonstrate a clear and unapologetic defiance of both the Nairobi and Luanda Peace processes.

a3672.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a3672.speech: “To this end, collective efforts are ongoing in line with the SADC Mutual Defence Pact of 2003, to protect the people of the region from instability arising from the conflict and to address security challenges in accordance with international law,” Magosi said.

a3952.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a3952.speech: Placed Mozambique “at the crossroads of multiple converging crises”, where the consequences of “delayed or insufficient” action are measured “not only in financial terms, but also in human lives and dignity” ; “Over the past months, the country has faced a relentless cascade of emergencies – worsening conflict in the north, recurrent and intensifying climate shocks (including cyclones and drought) and the resurgence of deadly disease outbreaks – all amid a persistent shortfall in humanitarian funding.”

a3952.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a3952.speech: Reports that, on the conflict in Cabo Delgado province ongoing since 2017, May saw the highest level of security incidents and violence affecting civilians since 2022, and that attacks by armed groups “have been happening in larger geographical areas and have shifted closer to main roads, disrupting movement and humanitarian aid” ; “Since January 2025, continued violence and insecurity uprooted over 95,000 people, many of whom still live in precarious conditions with limited access to basic services and protection. Over 700,000 returnees have returned to their places of origins but are still considered in need of urgent humanitarian assistance.”

a3952.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a3952.speech: States that Mozambique is “reeling from the effects of a prolonged El Niño-induced drought, which resulted in 4.89 million people projected to experience IPC Phase 3+ (crisis or worse), including about 912,000 at Emergency (IPC 4) levels in October 2024-March 2025” ; “The drought has pushed over 140,000 children into acute malnutrition and forced families into extreme coping strategies, including child marriage and survival sex” ; the three cyclones that hit Mozambique between December and March have worsened the country’s already prolonged humanitarian crisis.

a3952.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a3952.speech: “Mozambique is grappling with a major cholera outbreak, with nearly 4,500 new cases reported between October 2024 and July 2025 […]. Poor access to safe water, compounded by recent cyclones and weak infrastructure, has fuelled the spread […]. In July 2025, the country also confirmed its first mpox cases.”

a3952.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a3952.speech: Points out that women and girls continue to bear the brunt of the humanitarian crisis, as conflict and displacement have “drastically” increased the risks of gender-based violence, “including conflict-related sexual violence, while up to 75% of services for GBV prevention, mental health, and reproductive health are disrupted”.

a3952.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a3952.speech: “As of July 2025, the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP), which is seeking US$352 million, is only 19% funded, having received only US$66 million,” adding that “urgent and sustained” funding is essential to prevent further deterioration and to meet the growing humanitarian needs, which remain “as acute and widespread as ever”.

a3952.speaker: Center for Strategic Studies in Africa (study released in February)
a3952.speech: Found that at least 349 people died in attacks by Islamic extremist groups in northern Mozambique in 2024, a 36% increase compared to the previous year.

a4241.speaker: Célestine Zanou, President of the Dynamique du Changement pour un Bénin debout (open letter to President Boni Yayi)
a4241.speech: Hopes that Boni Yayi will take “the appropriate measures”, “with the sole aim of restoring the reputation of the Public Service and giving back hope to the young people who, with this competition, no longer believe in equality of opportunity in their country.”

a4241.speaker: Célestine Zanou, President of the Dynamique du Changement pour un Bénin debout (open letter)
a4241.speech: Wrote that since the memorable electoral knockout the country is inexorably settling into social, economic, moral and political chaos that even supporters of the regime acknowledge in private: “It is a red alert everywhere”, citing unequal social treatment amplified “against a background of nepotism, favouritism and above all a regionalism never experienced before”; “haphazard governance against a background of dictatorship that is destroying our dearly acquired democracy”; and a management of people “made of contempt and lack of respect for elders” ; “Mr President of the Republic, this country has a soul. Stop continuing to torture it.”

a4241.speaker: Célestine Zanou, President of the Dynamique du Changement pour un Bénin debout (open letter)
a4241.speech: Recalled extracts from her address of 31 March 2011: “Mr President of the Republic, if your first term is perfectible, the second must come close to perfect, because you will no longer have the excuse of not knowing the house well” ; “The term that is beginning will be one of all challenges... It is fundamentally a matter of seeking a perfect accord between word and deed. Be, as you proclaim, the President of all Beninese” ; “Thus, to better succeed in your five-year term, I advise you to beware of the incompetent and of the time-gnawers who did nothing to make your first term shine.”

a4241.speaker: Célestine Zanou, President of the Dynamique du Changement pour un Bénin debout (open letter)
a4241.speech: Warned that to keep silent in the face of the scandalous competition is suicidal and that history will remind everyone of it; challenged the President because “you do not have the right to continue to remain indifferent as is currently the case”, and said his “already too heavy silence could be labelled complicit if it persisted”; questioned the need for the commission of inquiry chaired by his Special Adviser for Political Affairs.

a4241.speaker: Célestine Zanou, President of the Dynamique du Changement pour un Bénin debout (open letter)
a4241.speech: Accused the Minister of Labour and the Public Service, Madam Mêmouna Kora Zaki, of having “deliberately turned a deaf ear to all proposals aimed at protecting our country from this scandal”, of having royally trivialised and ignored the alert from FESYNTRA-FINANCES, categorically refused its transparency proposals, and actively participated in the flagrant violation of article 23 of law 86-013 by taking an interministerial order on the eve of the competition; and listed irregularities including candidates associated with organising the competition, errors in the accounting paper, unsecured transport of scripts to secret destinations, delayed constitution of the marking jury, and two versions of the same communique.

a4241.speaker: Célestine Zanou, President of the Dynamique du Changement pour un Bénin debout (open letter)
a4241.speech: Demanded that the competition be cancelled “without any form of procedure” and that the perpetrators of the orchestrated schemes be “sanctioned with the utmost rigour” in accordance with law no. 2011-20 on the fight against corruption; asked finally whether the affair was “not staged to keep us occupied and to make us forget the challenges of the moment, which are named LEPI and the municipal elections”, and noted the letter would be copied to international organisations including the ILO, the AU, ECOWAS, the UN, the EU, the Millennium Challenge Corporation and USAID.

a4241.speaker: Mêmouna Kora Zaki, Minister of Labour and the Public Service of Benin
a4241.speech: Wrote in black and white that her collaborators falsified a communique after her signature, without her knowledge (letter no. 012/MTFP/SP-C of 14 January 2013 to the President of the OLC); claims to have nothing personally to reproach herself with in the file, yet refused the OLC access to the candidates' scripts (letter 25/MTFP/SP-C of 17 January 2013).

a4241.speaker: FESYNTRA-FINANCES (trade union federation, communiqués and letters)
a4241.speech: Having learned that the results of the competition were known in advance, made concrete proposals aimed at guaranteeing transparency (communique of 16 July 2012 and letter no. 020/FESYNTRA-FINANCES/SG of 17 July 2012 to the Prime Minister); made public on 27 July 2012 its position abstaining from participation in the commissions; asked the President for “the pure and simple cancellation” of the competition (letter no. 023/FESYNTRA-FINANCES/SG of 14 August 2012); and published tables showing that many of those admitted were of the lineage of the organisers (publications of 29 and 31 January 2013).

a4241.speaker: Director General of the Public Service (DGFP) and Director of Recruitment of State Agents (DRAE), in OLC questionnaires of 16 January 2013
a4241.speech: Are not unanimous on the place where candidates' scripts were marked: for the DGFP the marking took place at the Ministry of Labour and the Public Service, and for the DRAE it took place at the Technical Lycée for the large corps and at the Directorate for certain corps with reduced numbers.

a4241.speaker: Idjouola Agbèkè Yémangnissè Lydie (complaint)
a4241.speech: Her complaint, together with the disputed communique, made the whole world aware of the deception, serious irregularities, fraudulent manoeuvres, favouritism and discrimination that tainted the competition.

a4241.speaker: President of the Observatoire de Lutte contre la Corruption (OLC), letter no. 052/OLC/PT/SP/SA/2013 of 17 January 2013
a4241.speech: Sought access to the candidates' scripts, access which the Minister of Labour and the Public Service refused, in violation of decree no. 2008-180 of 8 April 2008.

a4271.speaker: Gunther Fehlinger, Austrian economist, Chair of the European Committee for NATO Enlargement
a4271.speech: Recently sparked controversy with tweets that seemed to threaten countries aligning with BRICS, using the NATO banner to do so; he later clarified his views as personal.

a4271.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopian Prime Minister
a4271.speech: Popular phrase, "We live as Ethiopians and die to become Ethiopia," encapsulating a desire for a strong and unified national identity.

a4294.speaker: Mohamed Malick Fall, United Nations Humanitarian and Resident Coordinator in Nigeria
a4294.speech: Said these humanitarian needs are “caused by conflict, climate shocks and economic instability,” speaking in Abuja at the launch of Nigeria’s 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP).

a4294.speaker: United Nations (statement/communiqué)
a4294.speech: The UN reports in a statement that Mr Fall was accompanied at the launch by the Federal Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, high-level representatives of the diplomatic corps and senior officials from various government agencies as well as national and international non-governmental organisations.

a4294.speaker: Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, Nigerian Federal Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction
a4294.speech: Highlighted the increase in humanitarian needs in north-western and north-central Nigeria and called for joint humanitarian, development and peacebuilding efforts for this region: “This will allow us to translate humanitarian efforts into durable solutions that will lift people out of poverty and provide them with livelihoods to achieve sustainable development” ; specified that the restructured Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction is committed to responding rapidly and effectively to humanitarian needs and poverty reduction: “We will continue to coordinate interventions at all levels, ensuring that they are aligned with national priorities on humanitarian assistance and poverty reduction.”

a4294.speaker: Babagana Zulum, Governor of Borno State; Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, Governor of Adamawa State; and Mai Mala Buni, Governor of Yobe State
a4294.speech: In their speeches, reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining collaboration with the UN and its partners in order to meet urgent humanitarian needs and promote sustainable development.

a4460.speaker: Agora Centre for Research (website)
a4460.speech: On its website, Agora Centre takes pride in “fearlessly tackling topics that mainstream media approaches cautiously”. It adds that “AGORA disrupts conventional digital tools usage, influencing social media to foster public discourse amidst tightening government restrictions on freedom of speech, assembly, and association.”

a4460.speaker: Sir Thomas More (paraphrased)
a4460.speech: To paraphrase Sir Thomas More, activist journalists need to start to ‘give the Devil the benefit of law’ instead of cutting “a great road through the law to get after the Devil”.

a4486.speaker: Jean-Noel Barrot, French Foreign Minister
a4486.speech: Speaking to France Inter, described the situation in Gaza as unbearable, referring to the blockade of humanitarian aid by the Israeli Government: "We cannot leave the children of Gaza a legacy of violence and hatred. All of this has to end, and that is why we are determined to recognise the State of Palestine."

a4562.speaker: Fitch Ratings (rating note)
a4562.speech: Affirmed Mozambique's Long-Term Foreign-Currency Issuer Default Rating (IDR) at ‘CCC’ amidst tight financing strains, a wider fiscal deficit and high government debt ; noted prolonged protests following the October 2024 presidential election translated into weaker economic activity, a widening fiscal deficit, and suspension of the country's IMF programme, impairing the government's ability to meet its high local-currency maturities in 2025 and 2026 ; highlighted that switch auctions on local-currency bonds, central bank borrowing and short-term financing are being used to service debt, but that large financing needs pose a significant vulnerability, and that declining external disbursements coupled with challenging domestic financing increase risks of spillover to external repayments.

a4562.speaker: Fitch Ratings (rating note)
a4562.speech: Said Mozambique's fiscal deficit widened to 4.9% of GDP in 2024 from 2.1% in 2023, mostly reflecting a decline in grants and some impact from post-electoral violence on revenue collection, and expects the deficit to narrow to 3.4% of GDP in 2025 and a forecast 3.6% in 2026, mostly driven by falling expenditure: “Financing constraints will contain capex, and we anticipate the public sector wage bill will fall relative to GDP. Nevertheless, budget rigidities will remain significant.”

a4562.speaker: Fitch Ratings (rating note)
a4562.speech: Said the government is exposed to accumulated external arrears to several bilateral and multilateral creditors in 2024 – including the IMF, Portugal and the Islamic Development Bank – with payments in many instances only resolved after the grace period had elapsed, but did not consider these incidents as defaults as external commercial debt was not affected ; said it understands the accumulation of external arrears to the official sector has continued in 2025 and that arrears on domestic bonds also remain an issue ; noted it withdrew Mozambique's Local-Currency IDR in August 2023 due to a lack of reliable information on the timely resolution of late coupon payments on unrated domestic government bonds.

a4562.speaker: Fitch Ratings (rating note)
a4562.speech: Said Mozambique's government debt fell to 91% of GDP in 2024 from 97.7% in 2023, mostly reflecting the out-of-court settlements pertaining to the ‘hidden-debt scandal’, and expects government debt to increase and stabilise at about 92% of GDP through 2026 and 2027, reflecting fiscal deficits and the rise in Empresa Nacional de Hidrocarbonetos' liabilities associated with Area 1, only partly offset by nominal GDP growth.

a4562.speaker: Fitch Ratings (rating note)
a4562.speech: Said real GDP growth significantly slowed to 2.2% in 2024 from 5.5% in 2023, mostly reflecting the broad negative impact of post-election violence: “We expect growth to only marginally rise to 2.5% in 2025, reflecting the contraction in 1Q25 and the dampening effects of FX scarcity on businesses activity” ; forecast growth of 3.4% in 2026 and 4% in 2027, mainly reflecting its assumption of a resumption in the construction of Total's LNG project in 4Q25.

a4562.speaker: Fitch Ratings (rating note)
a4562.speech: Said Mozambique's current account deficit will widen significantly to 26% of GDP in 2025 and 29.4% in 2026, from 11% in 2024, reflecting a jump in imports associated with LNG projects, which will be fully financed by investment through the financial account with limited impact on reserves: “We expect international reserves to remain broadly stable at USD3.5 billion in 2025 and USD3.4 billion in 2024, from USD3.5 billion in 2024” ; “FX scarcity has increased in 2025, partly due to a decline in external disbursements to the government and the suspension of USAID -USD586 million in 2024, equivalent to 3% of GDP” ; said the April increase in the share of mandatory conversion of export receipts to local currency (to 50% from 30%) will ease some of the FX scarcity, and assumes a new IMF programme and associated funding from the broader official sector will be announced over the forecast horizon.

a4958.speaker: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria
a4958.speech: Declared that he has a mission to unite Nigerians and assured Christian Communities in Northern Nigeria of his administration's commitment to ensuring fairness among all religions in the country: "I have a mission to unite this country, ensure its prosperity, and we are making progress"; urged the clergymen to have faith in his administration, saying that as leaders they have the responsibility to manage religious issues for the benefit of all.

a4958.speaker: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria
a4958.speech: Paying tribute to the mother of the APC National Chairman, Nana Yilwatda, who died at the age of 83, said: "In our family, we have a strong Muslim background, and I married a Christian, a pastor for that matter, and I have never forced her to change her religion." ; described the late Nana Yilwatda as a devoted mother during the funeral prayers: "The history behind this church is rooted in faith with deep acceptance in the Lord and tradition. I have been to Jos before. When we were coming here, Governor Caleb Muftwang showed me one of the bungalows, the house of Ambassador Yahaya Kwande. During the SDP days, we met there to decide the fate of MKO Abiola. Today, I am grateful that I am alive and to God be the glory to be the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and to come here to bid farewell to the mother of the community, and a humanitarian."

a4958.speaker: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria
a4958.speech: Affirmed his administration's commitment to tackling insecurity in the country, especially in the fight against terrorism and banditry: "We are defeating bandits, and we will defeat them. We will deal with them and combat the farmers-herders clashes"; stated that his administration is revamping the economy for the benefit of all Nigerians.

a4958.speaker: Nantawe Yilwatda, APC National Chairman and chief mourner
a4958.speech: Said his mother was a hard-working woman who lived on medication for 47 years: "I am here to thank God for her life. My mother worked for twenty-four hours despite her health condition, supporting us and providing humanitarian assistance." ; thanked President Tinubu for his emergence as APC chairman and promised to keep the trust.

a4958.speaker: Reverend Amos Mohzo, President and Spiritual leader of the Church of Christ in Nations (COCIN), speaking on behalf of the clergymen
a4958.speech: Thanked the president for his support of Northern Christians, especially by appointing them to key positions, such as George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, and Nantawe Yilwatda, national chairman of the APC; particularly thanked the president for his response to the insecurity in Plateau and Benue and urged the president to assist victims of conflict in Benue, as well as ensure the safe return of some Christian communities who fled Borno and Adamawa to Cameroun as a result of insurgent attacks; assured the president of their unflinching support in his administration's determination to actualise the Renewed Hope Agenda.

a5157.speaker: Guy Ogoubiyi, President of the National Anti-Corruption Authority (ANLC) of Benin
a5157.speech: Notes that the study was carried out in June-July 2014, with the objective of taking stock of the situation of transnational organized crime and documenting corrupt practices, highlighting their interrelations and interactions with transnational organized crime, analyzing the state of corruption, organized crime and the means used in order to better envisage enforcement, while assessing the obstacles and challenges in judicial procedures and questions of transparency.

a5157.speaker: Guy Ogoubiyi, President of the National Anti-Corruption Authority (ANLC) of Benin
a5157.speech: Expressed the ANLC’s gratitude to USAID for having helped make this study possible.

a5157.speaker: Team of consultants of the Laboratory for the Analysis of Social Dynamics and Development, headed by Professor Roch Mongbo
a5157.speech: Presented to the audience the substance of the special study on transnational organized crime in connection with corruption, which it coordinated and conducted.

a5157.speaker: ANLC special study on transnational organized crime and corruption (USAID-funded report)
a5157.speech: Found that the geo-socio-economic contexts of the West African sub-region breed corruption and illegality – low profitability of legal economic activities, weak State presence in border margins, systematic weakening of the State’s capacity to intervene; that the incidence of transnational organized crime is growing, involving drugs, weapons, goods, money and human organs, with children and prostitutes often the victims ; reveals that cross-border trafficking in human beings, notably children for domestic, economic or sexual use, is the highest form of cross-border crime along with drug trafficking, and that although a legal arsenal of national and international instruments exists, these texts are circumvented or have limited effect ; reports that the number of stalls selling pharmaceutical products in the Dantokpa market rose from 144 in 1987 to 1,000 in 2010, and that the share of overall petroleum consumption met by smuggling rose from 34% in 1987 to 85% in 2011.

a5265.speaker: Security sources privy to the matter (anonymous)
a5265.speech: Told Horn Observer that Mr. Fahad, who recently changed his name into Fahad Ahmed Dahir, has covertly travelled to Doha, Qatar on a flight via Addis Ababa, Ethiopia on Saturday.

a5265.speaker: An officer at the Somali military court (anonymous)
a5265.speech: "We can confirm that ex-NISA commander, Fahad Yasin had left the country. We have no further details," said one officer at the military court.

a5265.speaker: Supreme Court of Somalia (court record)
a5265.speech: Declined an application filed by Fahad's lawyers seeking the top level court to overturn a suspension decision on his parliamentary seat; the court found no reason to overturn the suspension decision issued by the electoral commission which refused to accept the initial victory claimed by Mr. Fahad for the seat number 086.

a5265.speaker: Hassan Mohamed, member of parliament from Jubbaland State
a5265.speech: "Having lost in the court application followed by the defeat recorded in the recent parliamentary leadership election, I think he senses the dangers unfolding. If Farmaajo loses the [presidential] race. That would mean less protection for him."

a5265.speaker: A lawyer working on the case (anonymous, due to security concerns)
a5265.speech: "The charges we are filing against Mr. Fahad include the disappearance and the murder of Ikran Tahlil Farah as well as several charges related to attacks, unlawful detentions, torture and injuries against journalists and members of the opposition politicians."

a5265.speaker: The Military court and the Banadir regional court
a5265.speech: Did not comment on the matter.

a5265.speaker: Lawyers working on the case
a5265.speech: Say prosecution against the pair (Kulane Jiis and Yasin Farey, both members of the new Somali Parliament) will require the court to write to the new Speaker of the Parliament.

a5265.speaker: Abdullahi Jimale, criminal law professor at the Somali university
a5265.speech: "Being a member of the Parliament gives you an immunity that provides a shield against criminal charges but that immunity can be revoked because this is the interest of the nation and it is the interest if the justice."

a5329.speaker: Malawi Congress Party (MCP) 2025–2030 manifesto (document)
a5329.speech: Aligns itself with Malawi 2063, uses disaster narratives to humanize the President, and paints a portrait of stability under the slogan “Taking Our Development Forward”; makes promises such as mega farms, ADMARC reform, and food security legislation without costed plans, timelines, or measurable targets; sidesteps the kwacha collapse, the 2024 IMF program breakdown, and the deep forex shortage; mentions anti-corruption conferences and judicial amendments, but avoids explaining how to dismantle political capture or recover stolen public funds; offers the slogans “Make Malawi Feed Malawi” and “Smart Villages”; celebrates the appointment of Martha Chizuma and legislative changes to empower the ACB; highlights increased CDF allocations and infrastructure builds.

a5329.speaker: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) 2025 manifesto (document)
