a5329.speech: Is framed in two phases: stabilization (2025–2027) and growth (2028–2030); openly confronts the hard truths that inflation must be brought down to single digits, public debt, now at MK16.4 trillion, must be restructured, forex reserves must be rebuilt in partnership with the IMF, and fiscal discipline must save K5.15 trillion by 2030; allocates MK6.35 trillion for targeted investments in energy, mining, infrastructure, and agriculture, and lays out a framework for Special Economic Zones; offers universal broadband coverage to 80%, AI integration in agriculture and health, a cybersecurity academy, and a national digital ID rollout; specifies irrigation expansion to 147,000 hectares by 2030, crop diversification strategies, and agro-processing zones; proposes depoliticizing key institutions, implementing lifestyle audits, digitizing procurement, and performance-based reforms in the civil service; embeds ring-fenced allocations for women (K100M per constituency), youth (K100M), and sports (K50M).

a5333.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5333.speech: Said he was “disappointed” with Musk’s criticisms of his administration’s centrepiece tax and spending bill, musing that it may be the end of their “great relationship” ; speaking to reporters during a news conference with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, defended the bill and said: “I’m very disappointed because Elon knew the inner workings of this bill better than almost anybody sitting here. All of a sudden he had a problem.” ; went on to suggest that Musk was upset about the removal of subsidies and mandates for electric vehicles, which could affect his Tesla business.

a5333.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5333.speech: Appeared to downplay the situation: “Oh it’s okay. It’s going very well, never done better,” he told news site Politico.

a5333.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (Truth Social post)
a5333.speech: Claimed that Musk “just went CRAZY” and posted: “The easiest way to save money in our Budget, Billions and Billions of Dollars, is to terminate Elon’s Governmental Subsidies and Contracts. I was always surprised that Biden didn’t do it!”

a5333.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5333.speech: On Jeffrey Epstein, said he knew Epstein “like everybody in Palm Beach knew him” but had a “falling out with him a long time ago”.

a5333.speaker: Elon Musk, former Trump adviser and head of the Department of Government Efficiency (X posts)
a5333.speech: Accused Trump of “ingratitude”, adding: “Without me, Trump would have lost the election” ; took credit for the sweeping Republican victory in last November’s election, writing: “Without me, Trump would have lost the election, Dems would control the House and the Republicans would be 51-49 in the Senate.” ; “Such ingratitude.”

a5333.speaker: Elon Musk, former Trump adviser and head of the Department of Government Efficiency (X posts)
a5333.speech: Called the bill a “disgusting abomination” and posted: “Shame on those who voted for it: you know you did wrong.” ; argued that the bill will irresponsibly add to the US national debt, and encouraged his followers to phone their representatives to express opposition to the spending plan ; denied he was upset about EV subsidies and wrote: “Keep the EV/solar incentive cuts in the bill, even though no oil & gas subsidies are touched (very unfair!!), but ditch the MOUNTAIN of DISGUSTING PORK in the bill.”

a5333.speaker: Elon Musk, former Trump adviser and head of the Department of Government Efficiency (X posts)
a5333.speech: Posted a poll asking his followers: “Is it time to create a new political party in America that actually represents the 80% in the middle?” ; reposted a tweet calling for Trump to resign, argued that his global tariff plan will trigger a US recession, and suggested without evidence that Trump appears in unreleased files related to late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

a5333.speaker: Elon Musk, former Trump adviser and head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a5333.speech: Said SpaceX “will begin decommissioning its Dragon spacecraft immediately”, but later appeared to back down from that threat, saying in response to a post on X urging him to cool off: “Ok, we won’t decommission Dragon.”

a5333.speaker: Elon Musk, former Trump adviser and head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a5333.speech: Appeared to believe there was a need to patch things up, responding to a post by Bill Ackman suggesting the pair needed to make peace: “You’re not wrong”.

a5333.speaker: Bill Ackman, prominent Trump backer (social media post)
a5333.speech: Suggested that the pair needed to make peace.

a5333.speaker: Karoline Leavitt, White House press secretary
a5333.speech: Condemned Musk’s Epstein allegation, saying in a statement: “This is an unfortunate episode from Elon, who is unhappy with the One Big Beautiful Bill because it does not include the policies he wanted.”

a5333.speaker: Congressional Budget Office (analysis)
a5333.speech: According to the most recent analysis from the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office, the spending bill working its way through Congress will increase the US national debt by $2.4tn over 10 years and leave nearly 11 million people without government-backed health insurance.

a5333.speaker: White House
a5333.speech: Disputes those figures, saying they don’t account for revenues brought in by increased tariffs.

a5333.speaker: Department of Government Efficiency (Doge)
a5333.speech: Claims to have saved $180bn, although that number has been disputed, and is well short of Musk’s initial aim to cut spending by up to $2tn.

a5333.speaker: Politico (news site)
a5333.speech: Reported that Trump’s aides have scheduled a phone call with Musk for Friday.

a5565.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Finance Minister of Tanzania
a5565.speech: "This is a strategic intervention designed to position Tanzania's economy on a higher growth trajectory, while ensuring more effective domestic revenue mobilisation," he told lawmakers ; according to the finance minister, the Act seeks to enhance tax administration while improving the ease of doing business.

a5565.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Finance Minister of Tanzania
a5565.speech: Said the government aims to strengthen the national response to HIV/AIDS and accelerate the provision of universal health insurance.

a5565.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a5565.speech: States that the Finance Bill is part of a broader strategy to drive growth in key social and economic sectors ; says the measure giving the trade minister authority to designate business activities restricted to Tanzanians only is designed to protect local entrepreneurship and promote fair competition.

a5565.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a5565.speech: Says the revision of the tax framework for two-wheeled and three-wheeled motorcycles and small goods vehicles is aimed at rationalising tax payments for low-capacity transporters, many of whom currently operate under loosely enforced regimes.

a5565.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a5565.speech: Says the reduction in excise duty on locally produced energy drinks aims to align tax rates with actual production costs and offer much-needed protection to small and emerging beverage producers.

a5583.speaker: Abdullah Saleh Saber, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Mali
a5583.speech: Says he is always ready to make his contribution to the process of root-and-branch refoundation, as a way of consolidating the gains achieved in the framework of strengthening cooperation between the two brotherly and friendly countries.

a5583.speaker: Abdullah Saleh Saber, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Mali
a5583.speech: For the ambassador, the borehole construction project is one of the many programmes carried out for Mali in various sectors such as health, sanitation and above all education ; these initiatives, he specified, reflect the depth of the relations between the two friendly and brotherly countries.

a5583.speaker: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (official commitment)
a5583.speech: Has been committed for decades “to promoting sustainable development in middle- and low-income countries and to reducing the economic gap that keeps countries under the yoke of poverty, undermines their capacity to meet the needs of vulnerable groups, and prevents their equal access to resources”.

a5583.speaker: King Salman Centre for Relief and Humanitarian Action (statement)
a5583.speech: “Acting on behalf of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Centre has helped to relieve the suffering of millions of people in need throughout the world.”

a5615.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a5615.speech: strongly condemned the attack that killed several Emirati officers at the General Gordon military base in Mogadishu on Saturday night; expressed his condolences to the government and the people of the United Arab Emirates and instructed the security agencies to conduct a thorough and urgent investigation into the security breach: “We offer our condolences to the officers who lost their lives in this terrorist attack in Mogadishu, those officers who came to our country to participate in the reconstruction of the Somali Armed Forces” ; “We strongly condemn this heinous act that took the lives of these officers who dedicated their time and lives to the liberation of our country and the rebuilding of our forces. We will not let this cowardly act deter us from our path of peace and stability.”

a5615.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a5615.speech: praised the UAE for its continued support in the reconstruction and development of Somalia, and said that the Somali people will always remember the role that the UAE has played in supporting their country in this difficult time.

a5615.speaker: The Somali government and its international allies
a5615.speech: have vowed to intensify their efforts to defeat Al-Shabaab and restore security and stability in the country.

a5770.speaker: South Sudan HIV/AIDS Commission
a5770.speech: Has announced the availability of Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) drugs enough to last for the next two years, contrary to a World Health Organization assessment that the country could run out of the lifesaving medication in just one month ; further revealed that Western Equatoria, Eastern Equatoria, Central Equatoria, Jonglei and Western Bahr el Ghazal are leading in HIV/AIDS infection rates.

a5770.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5770.speech: Warned during a press conference in March 2025 that South Sudan was among 8 countries in the world to run out of ARV drugs in the coming month due to disruption on the global HIV program.

a5770.speaker: Dr. Meg Doherty, WHO global director of HIV
a5770.speech: Listed Kenya, Nigeria, Burkina Faso, Mali, Lesotho, South Sudan, Haiti and Ukraine as the affected nations.

a5770.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director General
a5770.speech: Said the disruption in HIV program could undo 20 years of progress which would lead to potential rise in prevalence and fatality.

a5770.speaker: Dr. Esterina Novelo, Chairperson, South Sudan HIV/AIDS Commission
a5770.speech: Clarified that the U.S. foreign aid cut has not caused a significant impact, as the Global Fund will continue donating HIV drugs for the next two years: “The current global fund project that we are implementing through which we procure drugs for malaria, TB and HIV is ending in 2026. So we have like two years to go from now.”

a5770.speaker: Dr. Esterina Novelo, Chairperson, South Sudan HIV/AIDS Commission
a5770.speech: Narrated that health workers have resumed operations in their designated facilities, and encouraged people living with the illness to visit clinics and take their drugs: “The reason why we are having this conference is to inform our clients, all the people living with HIV, to go back and access the services they used to access. We have the drugs available, the doctors are there, the nurses are there,” ; “All the services are provided on daily basis. They should not shy away from going to the hospital because some of them still have that phobia when they found the clinics closed, that it means it’s not functioning. We have opened them and they are functioning fully and they should access their treatment without any interruption.”

a5770.speaker: Dr. Esterina Novelo, Chairperson, South Sudan HIV/AIDS Commission
a5770.speech: Said the commission has set up community interventions through volunteers working as monitoring staff and refilling the drugs for those who are unable to come to the hospital; she said the volunteers also provide care to those too ill to visit clinics.

a5770.speaker: Peter Garang Ngor, Executive Director, Network of Aids and Health Service organization of South Sudan (NASOSS)
a5770.speech: Revealed that only 200 out of over 1,000 health facilities in South Sudan have HIV services, and noted that little programs have been initiated to reach everybody to test and know their HIV status across the country: “We still have a vast number of populations in this country that do not know what HIV is, they don’t test HIV services, that are just left. They don’t protect themselves from HIV.” ; “The few numbers we have is an estimate and that estimate is drawn from only antennal care because we don’t have programs that reaches everybody to ensure that everybody tests and know the HIV status. So, in terms of the gap, we still have a wider gap because the government is not putting in any single money in interventions.”

a5770.speaker: Dr. Achol Ayom, Deputy Chairperson of the HIV/AIDS Commission
a5770.speech: Appealed to the national government to utilize the country’s resources to support the health sector instead of relying on foreign aids: “The government must to increase the budget of HIV commission, to increase the budget of health center. It’s like education, because education is part of us too.” ; “Because through the school we can spread the word of HIV. Community should be supported, because you remember our people, they believe in their chiefs. And I think this is one of the things we could use to reduce or to let people know what is HIV and how they can protect.” ; “The country is so rich. South Sudanese. We have a lot of money. We have gold. We have oil. We have so many things. Even our fish, water, we have it. Let’s think how we will support the health sector through our own, not depending on anyone.”

a5770.speaker: Mama Evelyn Letio, Executive Director, National Empowerment of Positive Women United (NEPWU)
a5770.speech: Said the PEPFAR program used to donate $1 million annually to the South Sudanese organization and accounted for 75% of the organization’s budget; revealed that within an estimated number of nearly 200,000 people living with HIV in South Sudan, nearly 70,000 rely on international assistance, and that around 70,000 people have been directly affected by Donald Trump’s 90-day suspension of U.S. foreign aid.

a5860.speaker: Transparency International, 2023 Corruption Perceptions Index (report)
a5860.speech: According to Transparency International's 2023 Corruption Perceptions Index, Ghana scored 43/100, showing stagnant progress in curbing public corruption. ; Norway ranks 4th on the Corruption Perception Index (2023).

a5860.speaker: Auditor-General of Ghana (annual reports)
a5860.speech: Auditor-General reports annually expose billions in misappropriated funds across MDAs.

a5860.speaker: OECD (studies)
a5860.speech: According to OECD studies, over 70 per cent of Norwegians trust their institutions - police, judiciary, parliament and civil service.

a5863.speaker: Tom Fletcher, head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a5863.speech: Said on Monday that Syria needed a "massive flow of aid" after the fall of President Bashar al-Assad ; "The situation is extremely dramatic" ; said the UN wished to "surge massive aid into Syria and rapidly scale up" its operations ; "Things are moving very, very fast" ; "the important thing is that the Syrian people now hold their destiny in their own hands" ; "The international community must stand alongside them" ; "seven out of ten Syrians need aid now" ; said the UN wanted to "do things on a grand scale" to provide "food, medicine, shelter, but also funds to develop a Syria in which the population can believe again" ; OCHA has "ambitious plans" for Syria ; "That will depend a great deal on the talks we will have here with the authorities."

a5863.speaker: Tom Fletcher, head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a5863.speech: Asked whether he would encourage the lifting of sanctions, replied that it was "still very early" ; "It is a very fluid time. Things are moving and we have to be flexible."

a5863.speaker: HTS (former Syrian branch of Al-Qaeda)
a5863.speech: Claims to have broken with jihadism.

a6064.speaker: spotlightnsp.co.za (report)
a6064.speech: According to spotlightnsp.co.za, in 2024 alone Ghana recorded 34,000 new HIV cases, while 8 million people were living with HIV in South Africa.

a6064.speaker: Elsie Ayeh, President of NAP+ Ghana
a6064.speech: highlights the impact of the U.S. government’s funding cuts, noting that in response nations like South Africa now finance nearly 75% of their HIV programs, showcasing a shift toward self-reliance; according to her, Ghana continues to underinvest in health, falling short of its 15% GDP allocation target, and she urges Ghana to leverage its resources and reduce dependence on foreign aid ; calls for African governments to invest consistently in healthcare infrastructure, encourage empowering language, and offer inclusive messaging; she advocates that media outlets should provide free airtime for HIV education and emphasizes that Ghana’s health systems should reflect its economic potential.

a6064.speaker: Elsie Ayeh, President of NAP+ Ghana
a6064.speech: highlighted the urgent need to end stigma in workplaces; references the Person Living with HIV (PLHIV) Stigma Index Study, which confirms that honest communication across age and gender offers relief and strength; champions peer-led disclosure teams, ideally composed of PLHIV, to support newly diagnosed individuals and encourage acceptance; questions why WHO’s educational materials aren’t widely circulated and calls for systems that ensure PLHIV receive timely, accurate information; stresses that education must go beyond hospitals into communities, supported by robust training for healthcare professionals.

a6064.speaker: Elsie Ayeh, President of NAP+ Ghana
a6064.speech: recommends increased use of local languages and documentaries in rural areas like the Savannah Region, where stigma is deeply entrenched; she cites delivery challenges, including patients avoiding public clinics and transportation barriers impacting medication access.

a6064.speaker: Elsie Ayeh, President of NAP+ Ghana
a6064.speech: says she has lived with HIV for nearly 30 years and embraces her diagnosis as her “second birthday”; she promotes a dignified shift in terminology — instead of people living with HIV being referred to as “patients,” they should rather be known as “Recipients of Care” — emphasizing wellness, a sense of agency, and respect. “We’re not sick. We’re living, contributing, and capable,” Elsie affirms.

a6064.speaker: Person Living with HIV (PLHIV) Stigma Index Study
a6064.speech: confirms that honest communication across age and gender offers relief and strength.

a6064.speaker: Daniel, 29-year-old person living with HIV, advocate with the NGO CPK
a6064.speech: emphasizes that proper treatment can prevent transmission to partners and future children; he’s concerned about declining international aid, especially following U.S. policy changes under President Donald Trump, and urges African nations to build internal support structures; Daniel calls for aggressive community screening, citing the Oti Region, where 15 new cases were recently detected, and that many are potentially undiagnosed; he proposes routine checks, early medication, and stigma reduction, equating HIV screening with normalized COVID-19 testing.

a6064.speaker: Charles, 28-year-old person living with HIV
a6064.speech: challenges traditional perceptions of HIV, stating: “I don’t feel sick—I’m very healthy. HIV doesn’t define me. I define how I live—with knowledge, love, and courage.” He pushes for government investment in healthcare post-donor cuts, noting that access to medication should be as routine as other public services; Charles actively clears up misconceptions between HIV and AIDS, underscoring the treatable nature of HIV with consistent care.

a6064.speaker: Moses, 27-year-old nurse living with HIV
a6064.speech: recognizes workplace stigma rooted in ignorance; he chooses to keep his status private, not because he is ashamed but as a personal boundary; based in Tamale, Moses educates others via TikTok and in-person sessions, advocating for widespread, early testing; he highlights the efficacy of modern treatment — usually a single daily pill — and stresses that undetectable viral loads greatly reduce transmission risk; Moses roots for normalization of testing and early intervention.

a6064.speaker: Malik, 28-year-old pharmaceutical technician living with HIV
a6064.speech: calls for non-political HIV program branding to ensure service continuity amid government transitions; Malik supports increased local research and warns against relying on rumored cures, stressing the importance of validated science over desperation; he said that in 2024, Ghana reported over 30,000 people living with HIV, with 15,000 new infections, including 4,118 males, 10,303 females, and 1,243 children (0–14); Malik values data transparency led by the Ghana Statistical Service and anticipates 2025 data will guide future interventions.

a6064.speaker: All five individuals living positively with HIV interviewed
a6064.speech: support ICASA’s upcoming conference in Ghana, lauding its efforts to unite scientists, researchers, and policymakers; they believe the event can reignite momentum for sustainable HIV care strategies and strengthen domestic health systems across Africa, and they particularly emphasize regional advocacy, education, and grassroots empowerment as the way forward.

a6064.speaker: Luc Bodea Armand, Director of ICASA and Coordinator of SAA
a6064.speech: stated that the ICASA program focuses on combating HIV/AIDS, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), tuberculosis (TB), and other emerging infectious diseases across the continent.

a6064.speaker: Prof. Muhammad Chakron, Vice President of the Society for AIDS in Africa (SAA)
a6064.speech: emphasized the importance of sustainable health systems and increased domestic financing.

a6064.speaker: Dr. David Pagwesese Parirenyatwa, President of the Society for AIDS in Africa (SAA)
a6064.speech: called on the African Union to increase funding in response to cuts in HIV support across Africa by the United States government. He also disclosed encouraging developments in South Africa, where groundbreaking research in the HIV Cure Trial has provided hope for a potential cure.

a6137.speaker: Fitch Ratings (report)
a6137.speech: Concluded that the prolonged protests following the October 2024 presidential elections resulted in weaker economic activity, an increased fiscal deficit and the suspension of the IMF programme in the country, harming the Government's capacity to honour its high local-currency maturities in 2025 and 2026 ; according to the agency, central bank loans and the issuance of short-term treasury bills are being used to pay State debts, but the large financing needs represent a significant vulnerability; foreign exchange reserves have held up, but external disbursements have declined, which, added to the difficulty of domestic financing, increases the risks of default on external payments.

a6137.speaker: Fitch Ratings (report)
a6137.speech: The document mentions a widened fiscal deficit: Mozambique's fiscal deficit rose to 4.9% of GDP in 2024, after 2.1% in 2023, mainly reflecting the impact of post-electoral violence on revenue collection. Fitch expects the deficit to fall to 3.4% of GDP in 2025 and forecasts 3.6% in 2026, driven mainly by a fall in expenditure ; “Financing constraints have suppressed capital investment, and we forecast that the public sector wage bill will fall relative to GDP. However, budget rigidity will remain significantly high.”

a6137.speaker: Fitch Ratings (report)
a6137.speech: Says the Government accumulated arrears on external debt service payments with various bilateral and multilateral creditors in 2024 (including the IMF, Portugal and the Islamic Development Bank) ; “In many cases, payments were only settled after the end of the specified grace period. Fitch did not consider these incidents as default, since external commercial debt was not affected. Fitch understands that the accumulation of external arrears with the public sector continued in 2025.”

a6137.speaker: Fitch Ratings (report)
a6137.speech: Mozambique's current account deficit will increase significantly to 26% of GDP in 2025 and 29.4% in 2026, against 11% in 2024, reflecting an increase in imports associated with LNG projects, in particular the resumption of construction of Total's LNG project; these imports will be fully financed by investments through the financial account and will have a limited impact on Mozambique's international reserves ; Fitch expects international reserves to remain broadly stable at 3.5 billion dollars in 2025, and notes the shortage of foreign currency increased in 2025, partly due to the fall in external disbursements to the Government and the suspension of USAID (586 million dollars in 2024, equivalent to 3% of GDP) ; the April increase in the mandatory conversion share of export earnings into local currency (from 30% to 50%) will ease part of the shortage, and Fitch assumes a new IMF programme and associated official-sector financing will be announced over the forecast horizon.

a6184.speaker: UNICEF
a6184.speech: Has reaffirmed its commitment to collaborating with Tanzania to uphold the universal right of every child to protection, enabling them to grow free from violence.

a6184.speaker: Ms. Sheema Sen Gupta, UNICEF Global Director for Child Protection
a6184.speech: "No matter the circumstances, every child has the right to be protected from violence. Child protection systems connect children to vital social services and fair justice systems-starting at birth" ; "Together with our partners, we are dedicated to enhancing child protection systems in Tanzania, ensuring that every child grows up free from violence and has the support they need to thrive."

a6184.speaker: Ms. Sheema Sen Gupta, UNICEF Global Director for Child Protection
a6184.speech: Noted that despite significant progress in Tanzania, societal norms still endorse practices such as child marriage and corporal punishment in schools, and that a large number of children lack birth registration, making them vulnerable to violence and abuse; praised Tanzania for simplifying birth registration services, which have significantly increased registration rates for children under five, from 12 per cent in 2013 to 68 per cent in 2023; highlighted that the child protection sector is often overlooked and underfunded, leading to persistent challenges: "Rates of violence and abuse remain alarmingly high across the world" ; said that with the support of partners funding UNICEF's Global Child Protection Thematic Fund, UNICEF has been continuously assisting the government of Tanzania in strengthening child protection systems.

a6214.speaker: Christos Christou, International President of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a6214.speech: Said at an online press conference that during the past year of conflict “very few visas were issued” for medical personnel to enter Sudan, which “drastically hampered the humanitarian response” ; Denounced: “This is a deliberate decision to block humanitarian assistance, violating international humanitarian law and the laws of war and putting the lives of millions of people at risk.” ; Said the land routes to the RSF-controlled areas in Khartoum “are not viable.”

a6214.speaker: Christos Christou, International President of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a6214.speech: Recalled that 25 million Sudanese need humanitarian assistance, an increase of 40 percent on last year, while 18 million face acute levels of hunger ; Said the UN estimate of 13,900 dead since the start of the war may be “underestimated” ; Illustrated that in West Darfur alone it is estimated that “between 10,000 and 15,000 people were deliberately killed in ethnic violence” at the hands of Arab tribes.

a6214.speaker: Christos Christou, International President of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a6214.speech: “The crisis in Sudan is widespread and growing by the day, but the humanitarian response is deeply inadequate. There is no doubt that there are enormous challenges in Sudan, but they are not insurmountable. It is possible to scale up the humanitarian response, and we know this because we are there.”

a6214.speaker: European Parliament
a6214.speech: Regretted that the Sudanese authorities “have systematically refused authorisations for the transport of medical personnel and supplies” to the areas controlled by the RSF, mainly to the Darfur region in western Sudan, which is inaccessible to humanitarian aid and has to be reached through Chad.

a6214.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a6214.speech: The organisation recorded “catastrophic levels” of malnutrition in some areas of Sudan ; According to MSF, the bombardments, drone attacks and use of heavy weapons have destroyed much of Sudan’s infrastructure, including health facilities, and it is estimated that only 20 to 30% of health centres are still operational.

a6214.speaker: United Nations
a6214.speech: Estimates that 13,900 people have died since the start of the war.

a6214.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a6214.speech: Announced at the end of last week the arrival of its first aid shipment in six months to Sudan’s Darfur region, blaming “bureaucratic impediments and security threats” which “made impossible” the humanitarian response to the needs of the Sudanese population ; According to the WFP, on 23 March 16 trucks with 580 tonnes of food products entered North Darfur through the Chadian border town of Tina and a few days later another six trucks with 260 tonnes passed through Port Sudan, the latter being the first aid convoy to cross the war front.

a6498.speaker: UNICEF (Communications Department statement)
a6498.speech: “These efforts enable the prefectural authorities to play a key role in promoting children’s rights and in implementing local child protection strategies, thus ensuring reinforced monitoring of field actions,” UNICEF states ; the institution stresses that to date 23 million dollars, or about 14 billion CFA francs, have been mobilised with a view to strengthening the Ivorian government’s actions in various priority sectors: access to drinking water, education, health, nutrition, and youth employability.

a6498.speaker: Yacouba Doumbia, prefect of Bounkani
a6498.speech: Expressed his gratitude to UNICEF for this support, which makes it possible to offer a more formal setting for meetings and official gatherings.

a6566.speaker: Peter Breedt, Durban doctor
a6566.speech: Reported that the water was dirty and smelled of sulphur at the time he surf-skied off Durban's beaches in 2012, after which he suffered from necrotising fasciitis.

a6566.speaker: SA Health Review (SAHR) 2016 (report)
a6566.speech: Concluded, based on research taken from government's own Green Drop waste water monitoring programme, that three-quarters of the water pumped back into South Africa's rivers by municipal treatment plants isn't properly treated - in other words, it is still sewage that is heaving with infectious pathogens - and that 986 municipal water treatment facilities discharge 2,100-million kilolitres of treated water into river systems every year ; reported that acid mine drainage is contaminating water supplies as acidic water from decommissioned mines leaches into rivers, with high concentrations of toxic heavy metals including cadmium, cobalt, copper, molybdenum, zinc and uranium, which can have serious health implications, particularly for kidney disease and cancer.

a6566.speaker: Study of rural groundwater systems
a6566.speech: Found that the majority of those tested did not meet national water standards and that the groundwater systems were of inferior quality compared to surface water systems.

a6566.speaker: David Hemson, researcher, SA Health Review 2016
a6566.speech: Reports that "Less than two-thirds of households rated their water services as 'good' in 2013," with households reporting being concerned about whether their water is clean, clear, tastes good and is free of unpleasant odours.

a6566.speaker: Durban doctor (anonymous)
a6566.speech: Told the writer a few years ago that she was seeing so many cases of gastroenteritis in her practice that she advised people to boil their drinking water.

a6566.speaker: US Centres for Disease Control (CDC)
a6566.speech: Estimates that about half of all gastroenteritis cases are caused by viruses.

a6566.speaker: Government officials
a6566.speech: Often assure the public that they conduct regular tests of the water in rivers and the sea (though they don't test for viruses).

a6566.speaker: Johnson Lin, Atheesha Ganesh and Moganavelli Singh, University of KwaZulu-Natal researchers
a6566.speech: Found, testing the water in the uMgeni River between April 2011 and January 2012, a very high concentration of viruses, including adenoviruses, rotaviruses, enteroviruses, herpes and hepatitis B in the water in every sample, which pose a significant threat to people's health yet usually escape undetected.

a6566.speaker: Johnson Lin and colleagues, writing in the Journal of Water and Health, 2015
a6566.speech: Note that "Routine viral monitoring is not required for drinking or recreational waters and neither is it required for wastewater that is discharged into the environment. This lack of a monitoring effort is due largely to the lack of methods that can rapidly and sensitively detect infectious viruses in environmental samples."

a6566.speaker: David Hemson, researcher, SA Health Review 2016
a6566.speech: Says "population growth and greater urbanisation will increase the demand for water supply in the future" ; adds that "Demand is anticipated to rise over the next 20 years, while the country's water resources are considered to be almost fully allocated - leading to an ongoing critical period in water management" and that "The 2016 water crisis, precipitated by the worst drought since 1933, has resulted in widespread water shortages that are increasing stress on an already challenged infrastructure."

a6630.speaker: Members of the UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Sudan
a6630.speech: Are alerting the international community to the intensification of the conflict and the consequences this will have for civilians; the mandated experts are calling, among other things, for an arms embargo to be imposed and for those responsible to be brought to justice.

a6630.speaker: Mohamed Chande Othman, President of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on Sudan
a6630.speech: Warned during a press conference in Geneva that “the conflict in Sudan is far from over.”

a6630.speaker: UN Fact-Finding Mission on Sudan (report presented 17 June to the 59th Session of the Human Rights Council)
a6630.speech: Noted the intensified use of heavy weapons in inhabited areas, the explosion of sexual and gender-based violence, the instrumentalisation of humanitarian aid, and targeted attacks on hospitals. The report denounces the repeated targeting of the Saudi Hospital in El Fasher by the RSF, and a drone strike on the international hospital in Obeid that caused six deaths; humanitarian aid is obstructed by administrative restrictions imposed by the SAF, or diverted by the RSF.

a6630.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a6630.speech: Warns of a surge in measles cases in several regions of Darfur: from the first cases recorded in Rokero in June 2024 through the end of May 2025, more than 9,950 patients were treated in MSF-supported medical facilities, including 2,700 severe cases requiring hospitalisation, and 35 deaths.

a6630.speaker: Mona Rishmawi, member of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on Sudan
a6630.speech: Deplores a situation that has become “a humanitarian emergency and a human rights crisis of unprecedented gravity”, in which international crimes taint all the parties involved: “It is inconceivable that this war is entering its third year without any prospect of peace.”

a6630.speaker: Joy Ngozi Ezeilo, member of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on Sudan
a6630.speech: States that “impunity is the fuel of this conflict.”

a6630.speaker: UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Sudan
a6630.speech: Urges States to respect the arms embargo, as provided for by Security Council resolution 1556.

a6630.speaker: Mohamed Chande Othman, President of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on Sudan
a6630.speech: Insisted on the need to avoid any complicity in the ongoing crimes: “We call for immediate action, for rigorous respect for international humanitarian law. Promises of protection are no longer enough, they must become reality.”

a6651.speaker: Centre for Public Integrity report
a6651.speech: Suggests that the renowned 2007 break-in at the Pelindaba Nuclear Research Centre was not a petty robbery, as the South African government insists that it was, but a coordinated and well planned attempt to steal as much as possible of the 485lbs of bomb-grade uranium ; "The first raider went straight to the electrical box, where he circumvented a magnetic anti-tampering mechanism, disabled the alarms, cut the communications cable, and shut down power to a portion of the fence and to alarms on a gate just 250 feet away - opening a path for a vehicle to exit." ; the report said that those who participated had special training, and that the raiders arrived on a night when they may have expected little resistance: the Emergency Center supervisor scheduled for duty that night used a wheelchair, but had arranged for a colleague to take his place, who brought along her dog and her fiance, Frans Antonie Gerber, an off-duty firefighter; security forces never confronted the raiders, but the dogs' barking - which led Gerber to spy the intruders and his girlfriend to call for help - thwarted the intrusion.

a6651.speaker: Government of South Africa
a6651.speech: Insists that the 2007 Pelindaba break-in was a petty robbery ; wants South Africa's nuclear scientists to keep crafting medical isotopes in order to kill tumours, not people, and does not want to give up the uranium ingots.

a6651.speaker: United States government / American officials
a6651.speech: Want South Africa to hand its weapons-grade uranium over for safekeeping as soon as possible ; believe that South Africa has a "crime problem", one which will lead to Pelindaba being emptied of its treasures, understand the South Africans to be close with Iran, and mostly understand South Africa to be incompetent, fearing that a second Pelindaba break-in would result in a terrorist attack.

a6651.speaker: Gary Samone (Samore), President Obama's nuclear terrorism adviser until 2013
President Barack Obama (letter to President Jacob Zuma)
a6651.speech: Sent a letter to the South African president detailing his concerns about the Pelindaba break-in.

a6651.speaker: A person familiar with the independent investigation (anonymous)
a6651.speech: Said that disabling the security systems was not simply a matter of pulling a switch, but required electrical skills and knowledge of the security systems.

a6651.speaker: Waldo Stumpf, nuclear expert who worked for the apartheid regime and for the Mandela and Mbeki governments
a6651.speech: According to him, the vault in which the uranium is contained is impenetrable.

a6651.speaker: Abdul Samad Minty, South Africa's ambassador to the UN in Geneva
a6651.speech: Told the Centre for Public Integrity: "The problem is you can't have nuclear-weapons states who feel they can have nuclear weapons and have as many as they want." ; his long-held belief is that it is impolite to tell a country holding a quarter of a tonne of bomb grade material to dump it when you are holding 741 metric tons of the stuff.

a6651.speaker: NuclearTerror.org
a6651.speech: "There are about 40 states with approximately 2,070 tons of weapons-usable fissile material, enough to make more than 130,000 nuclear weapons", while only eight states (un)officially have the bomb.

a6651.speaker: Xolisa Mabhongo, Group Executive Corporate Services at the South African Nuclear Energy Corporation (NECSA)
a6651.speech: In an interview secured by the Daily Maverick, was equally as emphatic as Minty. "This is our property," he said of the uranium. "What they should be worried about is the stockpiles of nuclear warheads held by the US and others. That is a threat to the world." ; reminded that South Africa was the first country to voluntarily dismantle its nuclear weapons, and is the second biggest producer of medical isotopes that treat cancer, that no one else has done this, and that there has been nothing in the way of reciprocity from the big powers that jealously guard their own arsenals ; stated that the terms of the 1970 Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) determined that those who did not have nukes would not attempt to acquire them, and those that did would get rid of them: "We have kept our side of the bargain."

a6651.speaker: Xolisa Mabhongo, Group Executive Corporate Services at the South African Nuclear Energy Corporation (NECSA)
a6651.speech: According to him, South Africa's uranium is under "24-hour guard" by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), and South Africa has signed an additional protocol to the IAEA, which means the inspectors can visit its nuclear sites unannounced.

a6651.speaker: 1997 report to the South African government
a6651.speech: Informed the government that the country would run out of electrical power by 2007.

a6808.speaker: Stakeholders
a6808.speech: have stressed that FP2030 countries in Asia and African nations, including Nigeria, should amplify action on the ‘Made possible by family planning’ campaign to raise $1 billion for family planning and secure new commitments for rights-based FP services.

a6808.speaker: Research (unspecified)
a6808.speech: research shows that family planning is an investment, not just an expenditure for governments, and it pays dividends.

a6808.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
a6808.speech: According to the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), for every dollar invested in family planning, benefits to families and societies are estimated to be at least $8.78, altogether generating N1.06 Trillion ($660 billion) in economic benefits by 2050.

a6808.speaker: Guttmacher Institute
a6808.speech: has found that every additional dollar (N1,603) spent investing in family planning would save N4,809 ($3) in reproductive, maternal, and newborn healthcare costs.

a6808.speaker: Dr. Samukeliso Dube, Executive Director, FP2030
a6808.speech: enunciated reasons that everything could be made possible by family planning, under the campaign ‘Made possible by family planning’ ; “At times, the method they want is not there, at times these services are not integrated, and at times they are denied or discouraged from using family planning by providers or by society – overtly or in a subtle way.”

a6808.speaker: Dr. Samukeliso Dube, Executive Director, FP2030
a6808.speech: lamented: “Now, international development fields are at a sobering crossroads – gender equality, access to contraception and healthcare, women’s health – due to global cuts in foreign aid in countries across the world.” She noted that this was evident from the conversations at the Commission on the Status of Women (CSW), and the recent Africa Health Agenda International Conference (AHAIC) meeting in Kigali. She made a passionate appeal. “As this is happening, I have one appeal: not to forget investing in women’s reproductive autonomy. Now more than ever, family planning is the smartest investment global development actors and country governments can make.”

a6808.speaker: Dr. Samukeliso Dube, Executive Director, FP2030
a6808.speech: posited that as governments now consider how they will reprioritise their spending, the community must act decisively to prove the catalytic importance of family planning on a global scale ; asserted, “We all know what is Made Possible by Family Planning.”

a6808.speaker: Dr. Samukeliso Dube, Executive Director, FP2030, and many experts
a6808.speech: believe this is because family planning is so foundational, it is often overlooked, and worse, neglected ; Dubem expressed concerns about the knowledge gap about what has been made possible.

a6808.speaker: Research (unspecified)
a6808.speech: Research indicates that achieving gender equality could take 132 years at the current pace, highlighting the urgent need for action.

a6813.speaker: Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, Coordinator of Congo River Alliance-AFC (coalition of M23 rebels)
a6813.speech: has said that they are open to a direct dialogue with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government to solve the root cause of the conflict. Nangaa revealed this in a letter released on Saturday and addressed to heads of state and government of the East African Community (EAC) and Southern African Development Community (SADC). In the letter, Nangaa believes that the solution to the crisis that has stayed for more than 30 years is a direct dialogue. He argues that the Congolese crisis in the east of the country whose main cause lies in the illegitimacy of President Félix Tshisekedi is political.

a6813.speaker: Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, Coordinator of Congo River Alliance-AFC (letter)
a6813.speech: reminded SADC States that Tshisekedi recruited Rwandan Defense and Liberation Forces-FDLR (accused of genocide in Rwanda) into his guard, in mining sites and the war front, without taking into account the resulting risks of extermination of the local population, mainly targeting Congolese Tutsi. He also protested about the involvement of SADC troops in the hostilities to fight alongside the FDLR in support of the illegitimate regime in Kinshasa.

a6813.speaker: Heads of state and government of the EAC and SADC (joint summit, Dar-es-Salaam)
a6813.speech: During the summit, the heads of state directed for resumption of direct negotiations and dialogue with all state and non-state parties including M23 rebels. They also asked the EAC and SADC Chiefs of Defense Forces to meet within five days and provide technical guidance on immediate and unconditional ceasefire and cessation of hostilities, provision of humanitarian assistance, including the repatriation of the deceased and the evacuation of the wounded, re-opening of the main supply routes, notably Goma-Sake-Bukavu; Goma-Kibumba-Rumangabo-Kalengera-Rutshuru-Bunagana and Goma-Kiwanja-Rwindi-Kanyabayonga-Lubero, including navigation on Lake Kivu between Goma and Bukavu as well as immediate reopening of Goma international airport. The leaders also directed that modalities for the withdrawal of uninvited foreign armed forces from the territory of DR Congo be developed and implemented.

a6905.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (World Refugee Day 2023 message)
a6905.speech: “Today, in the Kakuma refugee camp, I met Abdulaziz Lugazo, who chairs a cooperative of farmers producing drought-resistant crops such as spinach, okra and collard greens… Today he can work with other refugees and Kenyan farmers on land provided by the government, and he earns enough money to pay for his children's school books and uniforms.” ; “Kenya and Kenyans have generously hosted refugees for more than 30 years. Over the course of my countless visits to the country, I have been able to see the impact of the many positive and concrete measures taken to improve the living conditions of refugees and host communities.” ; “I am taking advantage of this particular visit to stress to the rest of the world that we can - and must - do more to offer hope, opportunities and solutions to refugees, wherever they are and whatever the context. Kenya shows that it is possible.”

a6905.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (World Refugee Day 2023 message)
a6905.speech: “Integrating refugees into the communities where they have found safety is the most effective way to help them restart their lives and contribute to the growth of the countries that host them. Concretely, this means ensuring that refugees can apply for jobs, enrol in schools, and access services such as housing and health care…” ; “The Kenyan government is ready to implement innovative and inclusive policies that will enable a large share of the half-million refugees and asylum seekers to work and live alongside Kenyans. This will foster self-reliance, economic growth and a reduction in dependence on humanitarian aid.” ; “At UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, we know that inclusion is the best way to support refugees in exile, to prepare them so that they can contribute to rebuilding their country when conditions allow them to return, or to thrive if they are resettled in another country.”

a6905.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (World Refugee Day 2023 message)
a6905.speech: “But host countries cannot achieve this alone. The rest of the international community must step in and provide the financial resources needed to implement these progressive policies. We have seen enormous progress in this area in recent years, thanks to the exceptional generosity of donors, innovative approaches to financing, and considerable investments by the World Bank, the regional development banks and other international financial institutions. But it is clear that more must be done.” ; “Many host countries… have the will to welcome and include refugees, but need far more investment and support to achieve it.”

a6905.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (World Refugee Day 2023 message)
a6905.speech: “Unfortunately, in today's divided world, long-term solutions for people forced to flee remain pitifully rare, leaving a great many of the world's 35 million refugees in uncertainty. That is why, on this World Refugee Day, I conclude by calling on leaders to live up to their responsibility to negotiate peace so that the violence stops and refugees can return home safely and voluntarily. I ask governments to increase resettlement opportunities for refugees who desperately need them. And I call on States to adopt policies that harness the enormous potential of refugees to contribute to the social, economic and political life of the countries that host them. We know all too well the cost of inaction: a world where forced displacement is at the highest level in history. We cannot allow this situation to continue.”

a7123.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President
a7123.speech: Has called on BRICS nations to champion urgent reforms to the global multilateral system and forge a more equitable international order, and warned that escalating geopolitical tensions, protectionist trade policies and global economic disruptions are threatening development prospects across the Global South: "We are, therefore, supportive of meaningful BRICS initiatives that improve the resilience of our economies as BRICS countries and those of the Global South and also strengthen the global multilateral system."

a7123.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President
a7123.speech: Reaffirmed South Africa's support for WTO reform and urged BRICS to lead efforts that ensure trade supports inclusive development: "BRICS countries must champion the reforms that are taking place at the WTO. We must redouble our efforts to ensure that trade supports development. Global trade must work for all of us."

a7123.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President
a7123.speech: Calling for a move away from the current "firefighting mode" adopted by most countries in response to the US' unilateral tariffs to strategic action, urged BRICS to finalise the BRICS Economic Partnership Strategy 2030 and commit to removing non-tariff barriers.

a7123.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President
a7123.speech: Highlighted Africa's role in shaping global trade, citing the African Continental Free Trade Area as a cornerstone of regional integration: "Our vision is of Africa that is the beating heart of global trade engaging the world not as a mere exporter of raw materials, but as a creator of value, a connector of regions and a catalyst for shared prosperity."

a7123.speaker: "Rio Declaration" (adopted at the July 2025 BRICS summit in Rio de Janeiro)
a7123.speech: Called for the strengthening of Global South cooperation.

a7132.speaker: Monitng (MonITNG), civic technology platform
a7132.speech: Has raised the alarm over the state of two public schools in Rafi Local Government Area - UBE Primary School in Gimi and Mamman Kontagora Technical School in Pandogari - describing the situation as "a direct assault on opportunity, dignity, and the right to education."

a7132.speaker: Monitng (MonITNG), civic technology platform (open letter addressed to Governor Bago)
a7132.speech: "The school has been in a horrible state for the past three years. The two existing classroom blocks were destroyed by a windstorm, and since then, nothing has been done to rebuild them. The pupils now sit on bare floors, under trees, or along broken verandas, exposed to the sun and rain. There are no desks, no blackboards, no roofs, and no learning materials. These children are simply struggling to survive, not to learn." ; "In the same school, over 5000 children have either been forced to endure these terrible conditions or have dropped out entirely due to the lack of classrooms."

a7132.speaker: Monitng (MonITNG), civic technology platform
a7132.speech: Added that despite several appeals by the Gimi community to both the Niger State House of Assembly and the National Assembly, nothing has changed: "The community has not kept quiet. They have written several letters and appeals to their elected representatives at both the Niger State House of Assembly and the National Assembly, but nothing has changed." ; "Despite the billions of naira budgeted for education in Niger State, including federal and donor support through UBEC and other interventions, schools like UBE Gimi remain in ruins."

a7132.speaker: Monitng (MonITNG), civic technology platform
a7132.speech: Reported similar scenes of abandonment and neglect at Mamman Kontagora Technical School in Pandogari, with students learning under trees amid caved-in roofs and broken walls: "We visited Mamman Kontagora Technical School in Pandogari, Kongoma Central Ward, Rafi LGA, Niger State, and were deeply shocked by the scale of abandonment." ; "This tragic situation has persisted for over a decade. Both the past and current administrations have turned a blind eye, despite repeated calls from the community."

a7132.speaker: Monitng (MonITNG), civic technology platform
a7132.speech: According to Monitng, the state has benefitted from huge sums of federal and international education support, including from the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) and donors such as UNICEF, DFID, USAID, the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), and the World Bank, yet the impact remains invisible in rural communities: "The Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) alone disbursed over N250billion in counterpart funding to states for the improvement of basic education infrastructure, including renovation of schools, provision of learning materials, and teacher training. It begs the question, Where is the impact of this funding in rural communities like Pandogari?" ; "Beyond UBEC, international donors such as UNICEF, DFID, USAID, the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), and the World Bank have supported Niger State and Nigeria at large with millions of dollars in educational grants and interventions. These supports were meant to uplift the sector, especially in underserved areas. Yet, Mamman Kontagora Technical School continues to suffer neglect. It is unacceptable."

a7132.speaker: Monitng (MonITNG), civic technology platform
a7132.speech: Is calling on Governor Umar Bago to declare a state of emergency in the education sector, noting that the crisis has gone far beyond neglect: "We are calling on the Niger State government to declare a state of emergency in the education sector. Children across the state are learning in inhumane conditions, or not at all. This is unacceptable." ; "The future of Niger State depends on the quality of education we provide to our children today. Technical schools like this are crucial for building a skilled workforce. The continued abandonment of this school is a direct assault on opportunity, dignity, and the right to education." ; "This is a passionate plea. Let us end this cycle of neglect. The time to act is now."

a7132.speaker: MonITNG (@monitng), social media post of August 7, 2025
a7132.speech: "EXPOSED!!! Dear Governor @HonBago We visited UBE Primary School Gimi, the only primary school serving the Gimi community in Tegina Central Ward, Rafi Local Government Area of Niger State. A clear symbol of the government's neglect of basic education in rural communities..."

a7147.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7147.speech: Lectured Zelensky, reproaching him for a lack of gratitude for American aid: "You're gambling with World War Three and you dare to talk to me like that?" he is said to have thrown out, according to witnesses.

a7147.speaker: JD Vance, US Vice-President
a7147.speech: Reportedly drove the point home, denouncing a "disrespectful" attitude.

a7147.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a7147.speech: "I do not negotiate with a killer," he declared, implicitly targeting Vladimir Putin, while demanding an "unavoidable bulwark" to guarantee peace ; refuses to sell off his subsoil, castigating a first draft of the agreement that he described as "old-fashioned plunder".

a7147.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7147.speech: For weeks has been multiplying his attacks, accusing Zelensky of having "triggered" the war and portraying him as an autocrat; sees the Ukrainian rare earths as an opportunity to "make profitable" the colossal aid given to Kyiv.

a7147.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a7147.speech: In return has branded his counterpart a victim of a "Russian disinformation fog".

a7147.speaker: Senator John Curtis (Republican)
a7147.speech: Praised Zelensky's "admirable tenacity" in the face of Russian aggression.

a7147.speaker: Senator John Cornyn (Republican)
a7147.speech: Brushed aside the label of "dictator" pinned by Trump on the Ukrainian leader.

a7147.speaker: X users (anonymous social media posts)
a7147.speech: "Trump literally reduced Zelensky to shreds in front of everyone," marvelled one internet user ; "It's a diplomatic detonation live on air," added another.

a7147.speaker: Witnesses (anonymous)
a7147.speech: According to witnesses, Trump said to Zelensky: "You're gambling with World War Three and you dare to talk to me like that?"

a7275.speaker: Amadoun Abba, Director General of the BRMN
a7275.speech: Recalled that his organisation works to promote the competitiveness of industrial enterprises through the implementation of restructuring and upgrading programmes.

a7275.speaker: BRMN (Bureau for the Restructuring and Upgrading of Industrial Enterprises)
a7275.speech: According to the BRMN, this latest phase (Relance II, 2023-2025) aims to revive Mali's industrial sector by improving its performance and securing a greater contribution to economic growth, exports, investment and employment, to strengthen the institutional, technical, economic and financial capacities of the industrial sector, and to improve the competitive positioning of Malian enterprises on the sub-regional and international market.

a7275.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of the BRMN
a7275.speech: Recalled that before the approval of the new Relance II 2023-2025 phase, the Minister of Industry and Trade had instructed that activities drawn from the Transition Programme for the Restructuring and Upgrading of Enterprises be continued.

a7275.speaker: Chairman of the Board of Directors of the BRMN
a7275.speech: "As directors, our role is key in proposing and adopting new solutions adapted to these challenges, in order to revive industry and support its sustainable development. It is our collective responsibility to commit the necessary resources in a determined manner to make this transformation a success," insisting that the board must go beyond conventional solutions by demonstrating creativity and innovation, so that the solutions developed will have a direct impact on the competitiveness of enterprises.

a7275.speaker: Members of the BRMN board of directors
a7275.speech: Indicated that the multifaceted financial and energy-related crises faced by industrial enterprises demand responsiveness and agility on the part of the BRMN.

a7369.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare (represented by Nse Akpan, Director of Port Health Services)
a7369.speech: Warned that funding gaps and limited healthcare facilities pose significant threats to Nigeria's progress in Tuberculosis (TB) control; noted that while Nigeria has made notable advancements in TB diagnosis and treatment, critical gaps remain in the country's TB response; said that funding challenges have been exacerbated by the recent withdrawal of USAID funding, which previously supported nearly 50 per cent of TB case detection efforts in Nigeria; and highlighted limited health facility coverage as a major challenge, noting that only 56 per cent of healthcare facilities provided Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course (DOTS) services in 2023 - approximately 23,000 out of 40,562 facilities nationwide.

a7369.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7369.speech: Said there are coordinated efforts by the government through the Sector Wide Approach to address the funding gaps: "To address limited health facility coverage, we are currently expanding diagnostic and treatment services through public and private healthcare facilities. Furthermore, we also leverage on other programmes to deliver TB services."

a7369.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7369.speech: Said the primary drivers of TB in Nigeria include undernutrition, HIV, diabetes mellitus, smoking, and alcohol use, with the working-age group (15-44 years) being the most affected; reiterated that eradicating TB remains a top priority for the present administration; and explained that the government has significantly expanded rapid molecular testing platforms for TB to advance its Universal Health Coverage (UHC) agenda: "The number of GeneXpert machines has grown from 32 in 2012 to 513 in 2024, while Truenat machines increased from 39 in 2022 to 372 in 2024, and TB LAMP equipment from 52 in 2022 to 275 in 2024."

a7369.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7369.speech: Pointed to gaps in childhood TB detection, revealing that only 63 per cent of the estimated 59,000 childhood TB cases in 2024 were officially recorded, and raised concerns over low enrollment in Drug-Resistant TB (DR-TB) treatment, with just 3,500 cases treated out of an estimated 9,400 in 2024, representing a 37 per cent treatment coverage: "We are deploying many innovations including the integration of childhood TB screening and treatment into Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health plus Nutrition (RMNCAH+N) programmes." ; "Moreover, we are improving access to DR-TB services through the engagement and capacitation of the LGA and community levels, thereby ensuring more patients receive timely care." ; said there is an ongoing DR-TB survey to determine its actual burden in the country.

a7369.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7369.speech: Noted that the financial burden on TB patients remains a significant challenge, with 71 per cent incurring catastrophic costs while seeking care, and said this poses a major threat to ending the TB epidemic in Nigeria: "Many patients face severe financial strain, often losing their jobs or sources of income, discouraging them from accessing treatment."

a7369.speaker: 2024 WHO global TB report
a7369.speech: According to the 2024 WHO global TB report, an estimated 10.8 million people developed TB in 2023, with 1.6 million people losing their lives and 12 per cent of the global burden affecting the most vulnerable - the children and young adolescents.

a7369.speaker: Walter Mulombo, WHO Country Representative (represented by Mya Ngon, Team Lead for Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases at WHO)
a7369.speech: Emphasised the need for a dedicated, fully funded budget to sustain TB control efforts in Nigeria, especially in light of the suspension of USAID funding; noted that increased domestic investment would ease the burden on affected communities and ensure the availability of essential commodities for managing TB patients and their contacts; added that too many people are pushed into poverty when they contract TB due to lost income, transportation costs, and other expenses, and that 71 per cent of TB patients in Nigeria and their households experience catastrophic costs related to the disease.

a7369.speaker: Walter Mulombo, WHO Country Representative
a7369.speech: "As a global health organisation, WHO will continue to provide normative guidance, mobilise resources for the TB response, and strengthen the capacity of health system and the community, working in close collaboration with all stakeholders to end the TB epidemic." ; "We must sustain the efforts, and the gains achieved in these past years to stop the spread of the disease and end the TB epidemic by 2035."

a7447.speaker: Jorge Santos, ENAPOR
a7447.speech: "At this moment, Enapor is already intervening, it is already carrying out the recovery of the platform. Shed 2 is already operational. Within a few days, Enapor will announce that this same shed can already receive fish from our national and international shipowners. So, we are recovering the platform, which was in a complicated situation; with the reversion it was concluded that interventions were necessary. The interventions are under way."

a7447.speaker: Jorge Santos, ENAPOR
a7447.speech: Asked about the announcement made in April that the Government was negotiating the sub-concession for the management of the cold-storage complex with three partners, said the negotiations are continuing, but stressed that the sub-concession will be carried out with the platform already operational. "The platform is being recovered and the negotiations are under way, that is, we are no longer at the stage we were at. That is why, as a precaution, we decided to recover the platform just enough, put it into operation under ENAPOR's management and, from there, negotiate calmly with those partners for its sub-concession, already with greater valuation of the platform itself."

a7447.speaker: Jorge Santos, ENAPOR
a7447.speech: Said that Atunlo caused great damage to Cabo Verde. "This case is in the courts at the moment. Cabo Verde had to carry out the reversion. There are guarantees that have already been called in. The case is also under way in international courts. And at this moment there is already an assessment, but the company went bankrupt, not only here; internationally the company also has a liquidation entity."
